knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Agents \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\) seek to minimize \(F(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n q_i f_i(x)\) over \(x\in X\subseteq\mathbb R^d\), where \(q_i>0\) and \(\sum_iq_i=1\). Agent \(i\) stores a primal copy \(x_i^k\) and communicates over \(G_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-space methods using local first-order oracles and neighbor communication; auxiliary local states are permitted, but explicit dual optimization variables are not the defining decision variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A decentralized primal first-order method is a collection of local recursions \((x_i^{k+1},z_i^{k+1})=\Phi_i^k(x_i^k,z_i^k,(m_{ji}^k)_{j\in N_i^-(k)},g_i^k)\), where \(g_i^k\in\partial f_i(\xi_i^k)\) for a locally available query point \(\xi_i^k\), every message \(m_{ij}^k\) is computed from agent \(i\)'s local history, and no update uses another agent's objective or state except through received neighbor messages. Its primal output is the block vector \(X^k=(x_1^k,\ldots,x_n^k)\); solving the decentralized problem means driving \(X^k\) toward the consensual solution set \(\{\mathbf1\otimes x:x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{u\in X}F(u)\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The family comprises neighbor-local algorithms whose decision outputs are agent-held primal copies, whose objective information comes from local first-order oracles, and whose nonlocal information arrives only through graph edges. Auxiliary trackers or memories may be used. The target is consensus of all primal copies at a minimizer of the aggregate objective.
equivalent_formulations_latex: In stacked form, \((X^{k+1},Z^{k+1})=\Phi^k(X^k,Z^k,G^k)\), with the \(i\)-th component measurable with respect to agent \(i\)'s local history and received neighbor messages.
special_cases_latex: Consensus descent, diffusion, gradient tracking, exact decentralized correction, and projected primal methods fit the family when their communicated variables are locally maintained.
immediate_consequences_latex: A centralized update depending directly on all \(f_i\) or all \(x_i^k\) is outside this family unless that information has been obtained through the allowed communication process.
boundary_notes: The definition does not assert convergence or prescribe a mixing matrix.
Primal-dual saddle methods may produce primal iterates but are not classified here when dual variables define the core recursion.

children.title: Distributed Consensus and Averaging Methods
children.top_down_role: Consensus mechanisms used alone or inside optimization methods.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(n\) agents hold inputs \(a_i\in\mathbb R^d\). Their states \(x_i^k\in\mathbb R^d\) evolve using messages exchanged along a graph sequence \((G_k)_{k\ge0}\). Define \(\bar a=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^na_i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact arithmetic and uniform arithmetic averaging; weighted averaging replaces the uniform target by a specified positive weight vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A distributed averaging method is a neighbor-local state evolution initialized from \(x_i^0=a_i\) whose designated outputs satisfy \(\lim_{k\to\infty}x_i^k=\bar a\) for every agent \(i\) and every admissible input tuple \((a_1,\ldots,a_n)\). Finite-time averaging is the stronger property that, for every admissible input tuple, some finite \(K\) satisfies \(x_i^k=\bar a\) for all \(i\) and all \(k\ge K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each agent begins with a local vector and uses only neighbor communication. The process performs distributed averaging if every designated local output converges to the arithmetic mean of all initial vectors for every admissible input. Finite-time averaging requires exact agreement with that mean after a finite round.
equivalent_formulations_latex: With \(X^k=(x_1^k;\ldots;x_n^k)\) and \(J=n^{-1}\mathbf1\mathbf1^\top\), distributed averaging is \(X^k\to(J\otimes I_d)X^0\).
It is equivalently the conjunction of consensus, \(\|(I-J)\otimes I_d\,X^k\|\to0\), and correctness, \((J\otimes I_d)X^k\to(J\otimes I_d)X^0\).
special_cases_latex: For \(d=1\), the process computes the scalar arithmetic mean.
Weighted averaging targets \(\sum_iq_ia_i\) and is distinct unless \(q_i=1/n\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If the iteration preserves \(\sum_i x_i^k\), then consensus at any limit implies that the common limit equals \(\bar a\).
boundary_notes: Agreement at an input-dependent value without mean correctness is consensus but not distributed averaging.
The definition alone supplies no rate or connectivity condition.

children.title: Linear Consensus Methods
children.top_down_role: Deterministic averaging over fixed or switching networks.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Matrix Consensus Residual Certificate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The mixing residual vanishes exactly at consensus, and the spectral gap bounds distance to consensus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W=W^{\mathsf T}\ge0\), \(W\mathbf1=\mathbf1\), and \(\ker(I-W)=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1\}\). If \(\lambda_2(W)\) is the largest eigenvalue below one, then \[(I-W)X=0\iff X=JX,\qquad \|(I-J)X\|_F\le\frac{\|(I-W)X\|_F}{1-\lambda_2(W)}.\]
assumptions_latex: \(W=W^{\mathsf T}\ge0\) and \(W\mathbf1=\mathbf1\).
\(\ker(I-W)=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consensus certificate for fixed symmetric nonnegative mixing.

knowledge_statements.title: Row-Stochastic Mixing Need Not Preserve the Arithmetic Average
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primitive row-stochastic mixing reaches Perron-weighted consensus and preserves the arithmetic average only when it is doubly stochastic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(W\ge0\) is primitive and row stochastic, there is a unique \(\pi>0\) with \(\pi^{\mathsf T}W=\pi^{\mathsf T}\) and \(\pi^{\mathsf T}\mathbf1=1\), and \[W^k\to\mathbf1\pi^{\mathsf T},\qquad X^k\to\mathbf1\pi^{\mathsf T}X^0.\] This equals arithmetic-average consensus for every \(X^0\) if and only if \(\pi=\mathbf1/n\), equivalently \(W\) is also column stochastic.
assumptions_latex: \(W\ge0\) is primitive.
\(W\mathbf1=\mathbf1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limit selected by primitive unbalanced deterministic mixing.

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Characterization and Linear Rate of Fixed Consensus
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Symmetric average-preserving mixing reaches average consensus exactly when every nonconsensus eigenvalue lies inside the unit disk; the largest modulus is the linear factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W=W^{\mathsf T}\), \(W\mathbf1=\mathbf1\), and let \(1=\lambda_1>\lambda_2\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_n>-1\). For \(X^{k+1}=WX^k\), \[(I-J)X^k=(W-J)^k(I-J)X^0,\qquad \|(I-J)X^k\|_2\le\rho^k\|(I-J)X^0\|_2,\] where \(\rho=\max_{i\ge2}|\lambda_i|<1\). Conversely, convergence to \(JX^0\) for every initial state requires all nonconsensus eigenvalues to have modulus below one.
assumptions_latex: \(W=W^{\mathsf T}\) and \(W\mathbf1=\mathbf1\).
Eigenvalue one is simple and \(\max_{i\ge2}|\lambda_i(W)|<1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed symmetric deterministic mixing; gossip and polynomial acceleration are excluded.

notation.meaning: Largest modulus of a nonconsensus eigenvalue.

knowledge_statements.title: Linear Consensus Methods
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Agents repeatedly replace their states by weighted neighbor averages. Doubly stochastic weights preserve the initial average, and contracting matrix products drive all agents to that average.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given initial states \(x_i^0\in\mathbb{R}^d\), stack them as rows of \(X^0\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times d}\). At each round choose the prescribed graph-compatible mixing matrix \(W_k\) and update \[X^{k+1}=W_kX^k,\qquad x_i^{k+1}=\sum_{j=1}^n (W_k)_{ij}x_j^k.\] Stop after a fixed budget or when \(\|(I-J)X^k\|\) is below a stated tolerance, and output each row. Row stochasticity preserves consensus states; column stochasticity preserves \(\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T}X^k\). If \(\|W_{k-1:0}-J\|\to0\), then \(X^k\to JX^0\), whose rows equal \(n^{-1}\sum_i x_i^0\).
assumptions_latex: Each \(W_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is compatible with the communication graph and satisfies \(W_k\mathbf{1}=\mathbf{1}\).
For average preservation, also \(\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T}W_k=\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T}\).
The matrix products contract the disagreement subspace.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iteration \(X^{k+1}=W_kX^k\) converges to the rowwise initial average under doubly stochastic mixing and disagreement contraction.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous deterministic linear consensus with fixed or switching doubly stochastic weights.

notation.meaning: matrix whose rows are agent states

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For \(n\) agents with states \(x_i^k\in\mathbb R^d\), let \(W_k=[w_{ij}^k]\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) respect \(G_k\): \(w_{ij}^k=0\) whenever \(j\ne i\) and \((j,i)\notin E_k\). Stack states as \(X^k=(x_1^k;\ldots;x_n^k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous deterministic linear mixing on fixed or switching graphs; affine, quantized, and randomized gossip updates are outside the formal core.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A linear consensus method is an iteration \(x_i^{k+1}=\sum_{j=1}^nw_{ij}^kx_j^k\), equivalently \(X^{k+1}=(W_k\otimes I_d)X^k\), with graph-sparse weights. It is average preserving when \(\mathbf1^\top W_k=\mathbf1^\top\) for every \(k\), consensus preserving when \(W_k\mathbf1=\mathbf1\), and doubly stochastic when both identities hold and \(W_k\ge0\). It solves average consensus on an admissible matrix sequence when \((W_{k-1}\cdots W_0)\to J=n^{-1}\mathbf1\mathbf1^\top\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear consensus method replaces each local state by a graph-sparse linear combination of current states. Row stochasticity preserves common states, column stochasticity preserves the aggregate, and convergence of the matrix product to the averaging projector makes the iteration solve arithmetic average consensus.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a fixed matrix \(W\), average consensus for all initial states is equivalent to \(W^k\to J\).
For fixed doubly stochastic \(W\), the disagreement recursion is \(X^{k+1}-(J\otimes I_d)X^k=((W-J)\otimes I_d)X^k\).
special_cases_latex: A fixed connected undirected graph commonly admits a symmetric doubly stochastic \(W\).
A switching method uses a nonconstant graph-compatible sequence \((W_k)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If every \(W_k\) is doubly stochastic, both the consensus subspace and the initial arithmetic mean are invariant.
boundary_notes: Row-stochastic mixing alone generally converges to a nonuniform weighted average.
Negative weights are permitted by linearity but excluded by the stated doubly-stochastic convention.

children.title: Gossip Averaging Methods
children.top_down_role: Randomized averaging driven by local activations.

knowledge_statements.title: Expected Mean-Square Gossip Contraction
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pairwise gossip contracts mean-square disagreement geometrically at a rate governed by the probability-weighted graph's algebraic connectivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let edge \(e=\{i,j\}\) be sampled independently with probability \(p_e\), let \(W_e=I-\tfrac12(e_i-e_j)(e_i-e_j)^{\mathsf T}\), and define \(L_p=\sum_ep_e(e_i-e_j)(e_i-e_j)^{\mathsf T}\). For \(Z^k=(I-J)X^k\), \[\mathbb E[\|Z^{k+1}\|_F^2\mid Z^k]\le\left(1-\tfrac12\lambda_2(L_p)\right)\|Z^k\|_F^2.\] Hence \(k=O(\lambda_2(L_p)^{-1}\log(1/\varepsilon))\) activations suffice for relative mean-square error \(\varepsilon\).
assumptions_latex: Edges are sampled independently with probabilities \(p_e\).
The positive-probability support graph is connected.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral rate for independent pairwise edge sampling.

knowledge_statements.title: Disconnected Activation-Support Boundary
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pairwise gossip cannot reach global average consensus when the edges that can activate form a disconnected graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E_+=\{e:p_e>0\}\). If \((V,E_+)\) is disconnected, every gossip update preserves each connected component's average independently. Initial component averages that differ can never converge to one global average.
assumptions_latex: Only edges with \(p_e>0\) can activate.
The positive-probability support graph is disconnected.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp reachability boundary for independent pairwise gossip.

knowledge_statements.title: Gossip Averaging Methods
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Randomly selected neighbors replace their vector values by their mean. The network average is preserved, and independent positive-probability edge activations yield average consensus almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), let each agent hold \(x_i^0\in\mathbb R^d\), and let \(X^k\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}\) have rows \((x_i^k)^\top\). At iteration \(k\), independently sample an edge \(e_k=\{i,j\}\) with probability \(p_{ij}>0\), and set \[x_i^{k+1}=x_j^{k+1}=\frac{x_i^k+x_j^k}{2},\qquad x_\ell^{k+1}=x_\ell^k\quad(\ell\notin\{i,j\}).\] Equivalently, \(X^{k+1}=W_{e_k}X^k\), where \(W_{\{i,j\}}=I_n-\tfrac12(e_i-e_j)(e_i-e_j)^\top\) and \(e_i\) is the ith standard basis vector of \(\mathbb R^n\). After a prescribed number \(K\) of activations, output \(x_i^K\). Every activation preserves the network average, and connectivity with positive edge probabilities gives almost-sure convergence to that average.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite connected undirected graph with \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\).
\(p_{ij}>0\) for every \(\{i,j\}\in E\).
The edge samples are independent across iterations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_i^k\to \bar x^0:=n^{-1}\sum_{r=1}^n x_r^0\) almost surely for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pairwise randomized gossip on a fixed connected undirected graph.

notation.meaning: Matrix whose ith row is the state held by agent i at iteration k.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be an undirected communication graph. Agents hold \(x_i^k\in\mathbb R^d\). At round \(k\), an edge \(e_k=\{i_k,j_k\}\in E\) is sampled according to a specified stochastic process.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical synchronous pairwise randomized gossip with exact arithmetic; block, broadcast, asynchronous, and lossy variants require modified activation maps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A pairwise gossip averaging method is the random linear iteration \(X^{k+1}=(W_{e_k}\otimes I_d)X^k\), where for \(e=\{i,j\}\), \(W_e=I-\tfrac12(e_i-e_j)(e_i-e_j)^\top\). Thus \(x_i^{k+1}=x_j^{k+1}=\tfrac12(x_i^k+x_j^k)\) on the activated edge and every other state is unchanged. More generally, a gossip averaging family consists of random graph-local matrices \(W_{\xi_k}\) satisfying \(W_{\xi_k}\mathbf1=\mathbf1\) and \(\mathbf1^\top W_{\xi_k}=\mathbf1^\top\); it solves averaging when \(X^k\to(J\otimes I_d)X^0\) in the declared stochastic mode.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each round a local random activation selects an edge, and the two endpoints replace their values by their pairwise mean while all other values remain fixed. The resulting random graph-local matrix preserves both consensus and the global arithmetic mean. A complete specification states whether convergence is almost sure, in probability, or in mean square.

special_cases_latex: Uniform-edge gossip samples each edge with probability \(1/|E|\).
Nonuniform gossip assigns positive edge probabilities \(p_e\) with \(\sum_ep_e=1\).
immediate_consequences_latex: For every realization, \(\sum_i x_i^{k+1}=\sum_i x_i^k\).
Only the activated endpoints can change during a pairwise round.

children.title: Accelerated Consensus Methods
children.top_down_role: Polynomial and multi-step acceleration of disagreement contraction.

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral-Interval Misspecification
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Underestimating the nonconsensus spectral interval can make a Chebyshev filter noncontractive.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A filter designed for \([-\beta,\beta]\) controls a mode \(\lambda\) only through \(|q_K(\lambda)|\). If an actual nonconsensus eigenvalue satisfies \(|\lambda|>\beta\), the minimax bound gives no contraction guarantee and \(|q_K(\lambda)|\) can exceed one.
assumptions_latex: The filter uses a declared spectral bound \(\beta\).
An actual nonconsensus eigenvalue may lie outside that interval.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stability boundary for Chebyshev consensus filters.

knowledge_statements.title: Chebyshev Minimax Optimality and Accelerated Rate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The normalized Chebyshev filter is minimax-optimal among degree-K average-preserving polynomial filters and yields inverse-square-root-gap communication scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(0<\beta<1\). Among real polynomials \(p\) of degree at most \(K\) satisfying \(p(1)=1\), \[q_K(t)=\frac{T_K(t/\beta)}{T_K(1/\beta)}\] minimizes \(\max_{|t|\le\beta}|p(t)|\), with optimal value \(|T_K(1/\beta)|^{-1}\). Moreover, \[|T_K(1/\beta)|^{-1}\le2\left(\frac{\beta}{1+\sqrt{1-\beta^2}}\right)^K.\]
assumptions_latex: The nonconsensus spectrum is contained in \([-\beta,\beta]\), \(0<\beta<1\).
Filters are real polynomials of degree at most \(K\) satisfying \(p(1)=1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimal degree-limited contraction on a known symmetric spectral interval.

knowledge_statements.title: Accelerated Consensus Methods
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normalized degree-K Chebyshev filter of a symmetric mixing matrix preserves the average and contracts every nonconsensus eigenmode by at most the reciprocal of the normalization factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be symmetric and doubly stochastic, suppose that its eigenvalue \(1\) is simple, and suppose every other eigenvalue lies in \([-\beta,\beta]\) for some \(0<\beta<1\). For an integer \(K\ge1\), define \[q_K(t)=\frac{T_K(t/\beta)}{T_K(1/\beta)},\qquad x^K=q_K(W)x^0,\] where \(T_K\) is the degree-\(K\) Chebyshev polynomial of the first kind and \(x^0\in\mathbb R^n\). The filtered state is computable by a three-term Chebyshev recurrence using one multiplication by \(W\) per degree. Since \(q_K(1)=1\), it preserves \(\bar x^0=n^{-1}\mathbf1^\top x^0\), and its disagreement satisfies \[\|x^K-\mathbf1\bar x^0\|_2\le \frac{1}{|T_K(1/\beta)|}\|x^0-\mathbf1\bar x^0\|_2.\]
assumptions_latex: \(W\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is symmetric and doubly stochastic.
The eigenvalue \(1\) of \(W\) is simple.
\(\operatorname{spec}(W)\setminus\{1\}\subseteq[-\beta,\beta]\) for some \(0<\beta<1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Chebyshev polynomial acceleration for symmetric average-preserving mixing.

notation.meaning: Chebyshev polynomial of the first kind.
Uniform magnitude bound for nonconsensus eigenvalues.
Average of the entries of the initial state.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(W\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be a fixed symmetric averaging matrix with \(W\mathbf1=\mathbf1\), and let \(J=n^{-1}\mathbf1\mathbf1^\top\). For a polynomial \(p_t\) of degree at most \(t\), multiplication by \(p_t(W)\) can be implemented using \(t\) graph-local mixing rounds and finite local memory.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed undirected network with symmetric mixing; acceleration is defined relative to ordinary repeated application of the same mixing operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A degree-\(t\) polynomial accelerated-consensus operator is \(P_t=p_t(W)\) with the normalization \(p_t(1)=1\), acting as \(X^t=(P_t\otimes I_d)X^0\). The normalization preserves the consensus component. Its worst-case disagreement contraction on a spectral set \(\Lambda\) containing the nonconsensus eigenvalues of \(W\) is \(\rho_t=\max_{\lambda\in\Lambda}|p_t(\lambda)|\). The operator is accelerated relative to \(t\) ordinary mixing rounds when \(\rho_t<\max_{\lambda\in\Lambda}|\lambda|^t\). A multi-step recurrence is an accelerated consensus method when its induced input-output operator has this polynomial form and strict contraction improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accelerated consensus replaces the monomial produced by repeatedly applying the mixing matrix with a normalized polynomial of the same communication degree. The polynomial equals one at the consensus eigenvalue and is designed to be uniformly smaller on all disagreement eigenvalues than ordinary mixing.
equivalent_formulations_latex: A three-term recurrence using current and previous mixed states defines a polynomial \(p_t(W)\) and is accelerated when the displayed spectral inequality holds.
The disagreement satisfies \(\|(I-J)P_t\|_2=\max_{\lambda\in\sigma(W)\setminus\{1\}}|p_t(\lambda)|\) when \(W\) is symmetric.
special_cases_latex: Chebyshev filtering chooses a scaled Chebyshev polynomial minimizing a uniform bound on a known disagreement interval.
immediate_consequences_latex: The condition \(p_t(1)=1\) gives \(P_t\mathbf1=\mathbf1\).
boundary_notes: Acceleration depends on the comparison class, degree, and spectral interval.
For nonsymmetric or time-varying matrices, eigenvalue polynomial bounds may not control the operator norm.

children.title: Distributed Descent Methods
children.top_down_role: Classical consensus-descent families and their bias regimes.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Agents minimize \(F(x)=\sum_{i=1}^nq_if_i(x)\) over \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^d\), retain \(x_i^k\in X\), and use graph-compatible weights \(w_{ij}^k\). Let \(g_i^k\in\partial f_i(x_i^k)\) or \(g_i^k=\nabla f_i(x_i^k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal consensus-descent recursions without a separate dynamic estimator of the aggregate gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A distributed descent method is a local recursion formed by a consensus operation and a local first-order displacement. In mix-then-descend form, \(v_i^k=\sum_jw_{ij}^kx_j^k\) and \(x_i^{k+1}=\mathcal R_i^k(v_i^k-\alpha_k g_i^k)\), where \(\mathcal R_i^k\) is the identity, a projection, or another specified primal feasibility map. Descend-then-mix uses \(u_i^k=x_i^k-\alpha_k g_i^k\) and \(x_i^{k+1}=\sum_jw_{ij}^ku_j^k\). The family is characterized by direct mixing of primal states and use of the current local first-order direction, without a tracker enforcing the aggregate-gradient identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: These methods alternate or compose neighbor averaging of primal copies with a local gradient or subgradient step. A feasibility map may follow the displacement. They are distinguished from gradient tracking by the absence of a separate state whose aggregate equals the current aggregate gradient.
equivalent_formulations_latex: In stacked form, \(V^k=(W_k\otimes I_d)X^k\) and \(X^{k+1}=\mathcal R^k(V^k-\alpha_kG^k)\).
special_cases_latex: Identity \(\mathcal R_i^k\) gives unconstrained distributed gradient or subgradient descent.
Euclidean projection gives a projected distributed descent method.
Constant and diminishing stepsizes define distinct bias and convergence regimes.
immediate_consequences_latex: With \(\alpha_k=0\), the recursion reduces to distributed consensus.
With \(W_k=I\), agents perform uncoupled local descent.
boundary_notes: The update template is a family definition, not a convergence guarantee.
Diffusion orderings can differ because mixing and adaptation need not commute.

notation.meaning: local primal feasibility or retraction map

children.title: Diminishing-Stepsize Distributed Subgradient Methods
children.top_down_role: Classical nonsmooth consensus optimization with vanishing steps.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Horizon Ergodic Subgradient Rate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A horizon-tuned vanishing step gives the standard order-one-over-square-root-K ergodic objective rate with a network-dependent constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under fixed primitive doubly stochastic mixing and uniformly bounded subgradients, run the distributed subgradient recursion for a known horizon \(K\) with \(\alpha_k=c/\sqrt K\) for \(0\le k<K\), and form \[\widehat x_K=\frac1{nK}\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\sum_{i=1}^n x_i^k.\] If an aggregate minimizer exists, constants independent of \(K\) satisfy \[\sum_i f_i(\widehat x_K)-\sum_i f_i(x^\star)\le\frac{C}{\sqrt K}.\] The constant depends on initialization, the subgradient bound, \(c\), and network mixing.
assumptions_latex: Local objectives are convex with uniformly bounded subgradients.
Mixing is fixed, primitive, and doubly stochastic.
The aggregate minimizer set is nonempty.
\(\alpha_k=c/\sqrt K\) during the length-\(K\) run.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex Lipschitz rate under fixed balanced mixing.

knowledge_statements.title: Summable-Stepsize Stalling
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite total step length can make subgradient descent stop short of the minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n=1\), \(f(x)=|x|\), choose \(x^0>\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\alpha_k>0\), and use \(g^k=1\in\partial f(x^k)\). Then \[x^{k+1}=x^k-\alpha_k,\qquad x^k\to x^0-\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\alpha_k>0.\] Thus positive but summable steps can fail to reach the minimizer even without network error.
assumptions_latex: \(\alpha_k>0\) and \(\sum_k\alpha_k<\infty\).
\(x^0>\sum_k\alpha_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-agent boundary showing why nonsummability is essential.

knowledge_statements.title: Diminishing-Stepsize Distributed Subgradient Methods
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each agent averages neighboring iterates and takes a diminishing local subgradient step. Standard nonsummable, square-summable steps yield consensus at a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Agent \(i\) initializes \(x_i^0\in\mathbb R^d\) and, for \(k\ge0\), selects \(g_i^k\in\partial f_i(x_i^k)\) and updates \[x_i^{k+1}=\sum_{j=1}^n w_{ij}x_j^k-\alpha_k g_i^k.\] Here \(W=(w_{ij})\) is a fixed doubly stochastic mixing matrix and \(\alpha_k>0\) satisfies \(\sum_k\alpha_k=\infty\) and \(\sum_k\alpha_k^2<\infty\). Stop using a prescribed iteration budget or tolerance and return the local iterates. If the aggregate objective has a minimizer and all subgradients are uniformly bounded, then consensus and convergence to a common minimizer follow.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) is convex and has uniformly bounded subgradients.
\(W\) is nonnegative, primitive, and doubly stochastic.
\(\operatorname*{argmin}_x\sum_i f_i(x)\neq\varnothing\).

knowledge_statements.title: Plain Constant-Stepsize Distributed Gradient Descent
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each agent mixes current states and subtracts a fixed local-gradient step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For differentiable local objectives and \(\alpha>0\), \[x_i^{k+1}=\sum_jw_{ij}x_j^k-\alpha\nabla f_i(x_i^k),\qquad X^{k+1}=WX^k-\alpha\nabla F(X^k),\] where \(F(X)=\sum_i f_i(x_i)\). Each round uses one neighbor-mixing operation and one local gradient evaluation.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Stability Test for Quadratic DGD
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For quadratic objectives, fixed-step DGD is globally stable exactly when its affine iteration matrix has spectral radius below one.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(f_i(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}H_ix-b_i^{\mathsf T}x+c_i\), with \(H_i=H_i^{\mathsf T}\), and set \(H=\operatorname{blkdiag}(H_1,\ldots,H_n)\). Then \[x^{k+1}=(W\otimes I-\alpha H)x^k+\alpha b.\] It converges to a unique fixed point for every initialization if and only if \(\rho(W\otimes I-\alpha H)<1\).
assumptions_latex: Each local objective is quadratic.
The stacked iteration has the displayed affine form.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^k\) converges uniquely for every \(x^0\) if and only if \(\rho(W\otimes I-\alpha H)<1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient linear stability condition for quadratic local objectives.

knowledge_statements.title: Penalized-Objective Representation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Plain fixed-step DGD is gradient descent on a quadratic-penalty relaxation whose penalty strength is inversely proportional to the stepsize.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(W=W^{\mathsf T}\) and \(I-W\succeq0\), then \(X^{k+1}=WX^k-\alpha\nabla F(X^k)\) is gradient descent with stepsize \(\alpha\) on \[\Phi_\alpha(X)=F(X)+\frac1{2\alpha}\langle X,(I-W)X\rangle.\] Thus every fixed point satisfies \((I-W)X+\alpha\nabla F(X)=0\), the stationarity equation of a quadratic-penalty relaxation rather than generally the exact consensus problem.
assumptions_latex: \(W=W^{\mathsf T}\).
\(I-W\succeq0\).
Each \(f_i\) is differentiable.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symmetric-mixing representation explaining constant-step network bias.

knowledge_statements.title: Constant-Stepsize Distributed Gradient Methods
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A two-agent quadratic example shows that constant-step distributed gradient descent can converge to nonconsensual local states, with disagreement proportional to the stepsize.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider two agents, scalar states, \(W=\tfrac12\mathbf1\mathbf1^\top\), \(f_1(x)=\tfrac12(x-a)^2\), and \(f_2(x)=\tfrac12(x-b)^2\), where \(a\ne b\). Constant-step distributed gradient descent is \[x^{k+1}=Wx^k-\alpha\bigl(x^k-(a,b)^\top\bigr),\qquad 0<\alpha<1.\] It converges to a unique fixed point whose average equals the aggregate minimizer \(x^\star=(a+b)/2\), but whose disagreement is \[x_1^\infty-x_2^\infty=\frac{\alpha}{1+\alpha}(a-b)\ne0.\] Thus a fixed positive step does not generally produce exact consensus, even for smooth strongly convex quadratic objectives and complete averaging.
assumptions_latex: \(a,b\in\mathbb R\) with \(a\ne b\).
\(W=\tfrac12\mathbf1\mathbf1^\top\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistent disagreement in constant-step decentralized gradient descent.

notation.meaning: Minimizer of the sum of the two local objectives.

Each \(C_i\) is closed.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Agents average neighboring feasible states, take local gradient steps, and project onto a shared closed convex set. Under the stated mixing, bounded-gradient, minimizer-existence, and diminishing-stepsize assumptions, they approach constrained minimizers and consensus.

knowledge_statements.title: Perron-Weighted Stationarity of Diffusion Fixed Points
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Perron weights and local stepsizes determine ATC fixed-point stationarity; a consensual CTA fixed point requires every local gradient to vanish.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Use the seed orientation and set \(B=A^{\mathsf T}\), so the combination is \(x^+=B\psi\). If \(B\) is primitive and row stochastic and \(\pi^{\mathsf T}B=\pi^{\mathsf T}\), then any consensual deterministic ATC fixed point satisfies \[\sum_i\pi_i\mu_i\nabla f_i(x)=0.\] A consensual CTA fixed point satisfies the stronger componentwise equations \(\mu_i\nabla f_i(x)=0\) for every \(i\), and hence also the displayed weighted equation. The unweighted aggregate stationarity equation is ensured for ATC when \(\pi_i\mu_i\) is constant.
assumptions_latex: The effective combination matrix is primitive and row stochastic.
Local gradients are exact.
The fixed point is consensual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_i\pi_i\mu_i\nabla f_i(x)=0\) for ATC, while CTA additionally requires \(\mu_i\nabla f_i(x)=0\) for every \(i\).

notation.meaning: Stationary left distribution of the effective combination matrix.

knowledge_statements.title: Small-Stepsize Stochastic Diffusion Neighborhood
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Small constant-step stochastic diffusion is mean-square stable, with order-step optimization error and order-step-squared disagreement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume the Perron-and-stepsize-weighted aggregate objective is strongly convex, local gradients are Lipschitz, the combination matrix is primitive, and sampled gradients are conditionally unbiased with uniformly bounded conditional second moments. For sufficiently small positive constant stepsizes, ATC and CTA are mean-square stable. With \(\mu=\max_i\mu_i\), \[\limsup_{k\to\infty}\sum_i\mathbb E\|x_i^k-x^\star\|^2=O(\mu),\qquad \limsup_{k\to\infty}\sum_i\mathbb E\|x_i^k-\bar x^k\|^2=O(\mu^2).\] Persistent gradient noise therefore prevents exact last-iterate convergence at a fixed positive stepsize.
assumptions_latex: The weighted aggregate objective is strongly convex.
Local gradients are Lipschitz.
Samples are conditionally unbiased with uniformly bounded conditional second moments.
Mixing is primitive and all constant stepsizes are sufficiently small.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Qualitative constant-step mean-square stability for ATC and CTA diffusion.

knowledge_statements.title: Diffusion Adaptation Methods
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Diffusion methods either adapt locally before mixing or mix before adapting. Both use neighborhood-weighted combinations and local exact or sampled gradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A=(a_{\ell i})\) be nonnegative with \(\sum_\ell a_{\ell i}=1\) and \(a_{\ell i}=0\) outside agent \(i\)'s neighborhood. Adapt-then-combine diffusion uses \[\psi_i^k=x_i^k-\mu_i g_i(x_i^k),\qquad x_i^{k+1}=\sum_\ell a_{\ell i}\psi_\ell^k.\] Combine-then-adapt diffusion instead uses \[\phi_i^k=\sum_\ell a_{\ell i}x_\ell^k,\qquad x_i^{k+1}=\phi_i^k-\mu_i g_i(\phi_i^k).\] Here \(g_i\) may be an exact or sampled local gradient. Initialize arbitrary local states, stop under a prescribed budget or residual rule, and output the final local states.
assumptions_latex: Each \(g_i\) is a local gradient or stochastic gradient oracle.
\(A\) respects the communication graph and has unit column sums.
\(\mu_i>0\) is agent i's stepsize.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed recursions respectively define the adapt-then-combine and combine-then-adapt diffusion families.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Balanced mixing cannot repair a wrong aggregate tracker initialization; the permanent offset can drive motion on a zero objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:

knowledge_statements.title: Common Noise Defeats Network Variance Reduction
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Perfectly correlated local noises are not attenuated by adding agents, so the average tracker retains the full noise variance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\varepsilon_i^k=z^k\) for every agent, where \(\mathbb E[z^k\mid\mathcal F_k]=0\) and \(\mathbb E[\|z^k\|^2\mid\mathcal F_k]=\sigma^2>0\). Then \[\frac1n\sum_i\varepsilon_i^k=z^k,\qquad \mathbb E\left[\left\|\frac1n\sum_i\varepsilon_i^k\right\|^2\middle|\mathcal F_k\right]=\sigma^2,\] independently of \(n\).
assumptions_latex: All agents receive the same conditionally centered square-integrable noise realization.
Its conditional second moment is \(\sigma^2>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp correlated-noise example for the average tracker.

notation.meaning: common noise shared by all agents

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Agent Noise Covariance Controls Averaging
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Network averaging reduces gradient-noise variance only to the extent that cross-agent covariances cancel.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\bar\varepsilon^k=n^{-1}\sum_i\varepsilon_i^k\), with conditionally centered square-integrable vector noises. Then \[\mathbb E[\|\bar\varepsilon^k\|^2\mid\mathcal F_k]=\frac1{n^2}\sum_{i=1}^n\sum_{j=1}^n\mathbb E[\langle\varepsilon_i^k,\varepsilon_j^k\rangle\mid\mathcal F_k].\] Hence the \(1/n\) variance reduction in the seed follows from vanishing cross terms and does not follow from centered marginals alone.
assumptions_latex: Each noise is square integrable and conditionally centered.
No conditional independence assumption is imposed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact second-moment representation replacing the independent-noise simplification.

knowledge_statements.title: Tracking under Gradient Noise
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gradient tracking preserves the sum of noisy gradients, not true gradients. Independent centered noise leaves average tracker variance of order one over the network size.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g_i^k=\nabla f_i(x_i^k)+\varepsilon_i^k\), initialize \(y_i^0=g_i^0\), and use \[y^{k+1}=Wy^k+g^{k+1}-g^k\] with a doubly stochastic \(W\). Then the telescoping identity \(\sum_i y_i^k=\sum_i g_i^k\) holds pathwise. Consequently, the average tracker equals \[\bar y^k=\frac1n\sum_i\nabla f_i(x_i^k)+\frac1n\sum_i\varepsilon_i^k,\] rather than the exact average gradient. If the noises are conditionally independent, centered, and satisfy \(\mathbb E[\|\varepsilon_i^k\|^2\mid\mathcal F_k]\le\sigma^2\), then the mean-square average tracking noise is at most \(\sigma^2/n\).
assumptions_latex: \(W\) is doubly stochastic and \(y^0=g^0\).
\(\mathbb E[\varepsilon_i^k\mid\mathcal F_k]=0\) and noises are conditionally independent across agents.
\(\mathbb E[\|\varepsilon_i^k\|^2\mid\mathcal F_k]\le\sigma^2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact tracking invariant and residual variance under additive gradient noise.

knowledge_statements.title: Random Reshuffling Is Not Per-Step Unbiased
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Random reshuffling is uniform over the remaining components, so its within-epoch gradient is generally not conditionally unbiased for the full local gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
During a random-reshuffling epoch, let \(S_k\) be the component indices not yet visited. Conditional on the within-epoch history, \[\mathbb E[
abla f_{i\xi_i^k}(x_i^k)\mid\mathcal F_k]= rac1{|S_k|}\sum_{j\in S_k}
abla f_{ij}(x_i^k),\] which generally differs from \(
abla f_i(x_i^k)=m_i^{-1}\sum_j
abla f_{ij}(x_i^k)\). Thus with-replacement martingale-difference arguments do not apply stepwise without modification.
assumptions_latex: A uniformly random permutation is traversed without replacement within each epoch.
The conditioning history reveals the indices already visited.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbb E[g_i^k\mid\mathcal F_k]\ne\nabla f_i(x_i^k)\quad\text{in general within an epoch}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional-bias boundary within a without-replacement epoch.

notation.meaning: indices remaining in the current reshuffling epoch

knowledge_statements.title: Conditional Variance of Importance-Weighted Component Sampling
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Importance sampling is unbiased, and probabilities proportional to nonzero component-gradient norms minimize its conditional second moment at a fixed iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At fixed \(x\), write \(a_j=\nabla f_{ij}(x)\), \(\bar a=m_i^{-1}\sum_j a_j\), and sample \(J\) with \(p_j>0\). For \(g=a_J/(m_ip_J)\), \[\mathbb E\|g-\bar a\|^2=\frac1{m_i^2}\sum_{j=1}^{m_i}\frac{\|a_j\|^2}{p_j}-\|\bar a\|^2.\] If every \(a_j\ne0\), this is minimized by \(p_j=\|a_j\|/\sum_\ell\|a_\ell\|\). If some \(a_j=0\) while strict positivity is required, the same value is an infimum approached by assigning those indices arbitrarily small positive mass.
assumptions_latex: The component gradients exist at the fixed iterate.
Sampling probabilities are strictly positive and sum to one.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact one-sample variance formula and variance-minimizing probabilities at a fixed local iterate.

notation.meaning: component gradient at the fixed local iterate

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Sum Sampling Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local finite sum may be sampled using conditionally independent draws, shared randomness, or random reshuffling. For a draw having the stated conditional probabilities, importance weighting makes the sampled gradient conditionally unbiased.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let agents be indexed by \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\). Agent \(i\) holds \(m_i\) differentiable component functions \(f_{ij}:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) and has local objective \(f_i(x)=m_i^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{m_i}f_{ij}(x)\). Let \(\mathcal F_k\) denote the history before iteration-\(k\) sampling, with \(x_i^k\) measurable with respect to \(\mathcal F_k\). Independent sampling uses indices that are conditionally independent across agents, with fresh draws over iterations. Common-randomness sampling uses a shared random variable or seed that may induce dependence among the agents' indices. Random reshuffling draws a permutation of \(\{1,\ldots,m_i\}\) for each local epoch and visits every component once in that order. If \(\mathbb P(\xi_i^k=j\mid\mathcal F_k)=p_{ij}>0\), then the importance-weighted estimator \(g_i^k=(m_i p_{i\xi_i^k})^{-1}\nabla f_{i\xi_i^k}(x_i^k)\) satisfies \(\mathbb E[g_i^k\mid\mathcal F_k]=\nabla f_i(x_i^k)\).
assumptions_latex: \(n,d,m_i\) are positive integers, and \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\).
Each \(f_{ij}:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) is differentiable.
The iterate \(x_i^k\) is \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable, and \(\mathbb P(\xi_i^k=j\mid\mathcal F_k)=p_{ij}>0\) with \(\sum_{j=1}^{m_i}p_{ij}=1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sampling conventions for local finite-sum objectives in gradient-tracking methods.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\), let \(X=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\in(\mathbb R^d)^n\), and let \(W\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be a mixing matrix satisfying \(W\mathbf1=\mathbf1\). Consensus is \((I-W)X=0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An exact decentralized correction method is an iteration on a primal state \(X^k\) and correction state \(C^k\) of the form \(X^{k+1}=\mathcal M_W(X^k-\alpha G(X^k))+C^k\), \(C^{k+1}=\mathcal U_W(C^k,X^{k+1},X^k,G(X^k),G(X^{k-1}))\), with fixed \(\alpha>0\), where \(G(X)=(

abla f_i(x_i^\infty)=0\); hence \(X^\infty=\mathbf1(x^\star)^	op\) with \(x^\star\) stationary for \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact decentralized correction method augments mixed local-gradient descent with a correction state. knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X^k\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}\), \(G(X^k)\) stack local gradients, \(W\mathbf1=\mathbf1\), and \(\alpha>0\). Define a provisional mixed-gradient update \(Z^{k+1}=WX^k-\alpha G(X^k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A structural family definition covering two-step primal recursions whose correction is the difference of consecutive provisional network updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A successive-difference exact-correction method is a second-order recursion initialized by \(X^1=Z^1\) and, for \(k\ge1\), defined by \(X^{k+1}=X^k+Z^{k+1}-\widetilde Z^k\), where \(Z^{k+1}=A X^k-\alpha G(X^k)\) and \(\widetilde Z^k=B X^{k-1}-\alpha G(X^{k-1})\) for network-compatible linear maps \(A,B\). Equivalently, \(X^{k+1}=(I+A)X^k-BX^{k-1}-\alpha\bigl(G(X^k)-G(X^{k-1})\bigr)\). The family is exact-correcting when its stationary equations imply consensus and aggregate stationarity rather than the biased equation \((I-W)X+\alpha G(X)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This family consists of two-step decentralized recursions that add the difference between a current provisional network-gradient update and a preceding provisional update. The resulting recursion contains a difference of successive local gradients, and its admissible network operators are chosen so that stationary states satisfy consensus and aggregate stationarity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The defining recurrence is \(X^{k+1}=(I+A)X^k-BX^{k-1}-\alpha(G(X^k)-G(X^{k-1}))\), together with the exact fixed-point conditions.

Explicit Unstable Quadratic EXTRA Instance
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even with two connected agents and identical strongly convex quadratics, canonically initialized EXTRA diverges or oscillates when its stepsize is too large.

Initialize \(X^0=c\mathbf1\), \(c\ne0\), and set \(X^1=WX^0-\alpha\nabla f(X^0)=(1-\alpha q)c\mathbf1\). The EXTRA recurrence remains in the consensus subspace and satisfies \(X^k=(1-\alpha q)^kc\mathbf1\). Therefore \(\alpha q>2\) gives divergence, while \(\alpha q=2\) gives a nonconvergent sign oscillation.

knowledge_statements.title: EXTRA Method Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical smooth unconstrained EXTRA recursion on a static undirected network.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F(X)=\sum_{i=1}^nf_i(x_i)\), let \(W\) and \(\widetilde W\) be symmetric mixing matrices, and write \(\mathbf W=W\otimes I_d\) and \(\widetilde{\mathbf W}=\widetilde W\otimes I_d\). From arbitrary \(X^0\), set
\[
X^1=\mathbf W X^0-\alpha\nabla F(X^0),
\]
and, for \(k\geq0\), update
\[
X^{k+2}=(I+\mathbf W)X^{k+1}-\widetilde{\mathbf W}X^k-\alpha\bigl(\nabla F(X^{k+1})-\nabla F(X^k)\bigr).
\]
The standard choice is \(\widetilde W=(I+W)/2\). The successive gradient difference supplies the correction absent from ordinary decentralized gradient descent; output the local blocks of the last iterate.

knowledge_statements.title: Vanishing Update Differences Are Not an Optimality Certificate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero update difference can occur at a nonconsensual or nonstationary state.

knowledge_statements.title: Telescoping Successive-Correction Identity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Successive first-order differences telescope to an endpoint difference but do not alone imply stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\Delta G^k=G(X^k)-G(X^{k-1})\), \[\sum_{k=1}^{K}\Delta G^k=G(X^K)-G(X^0).\] Thus accumulation of a successive-difference correction depends only on endpoint first-order maps; aggregate stationarity still requires a method-specific initialization invariant.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact State-Difference Normal Form

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be a nonnegative network mixing matrix and \(\bar A=(I+A)/2\). Agent \(i\) holds \(w_i^k,\psi_i^k,\phi_i^k\in\mathbb R^d\), a local loss \(f_i\), and a stepsize \(\mu_i>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adapt-then-correct-then-combine exact-diffusion structure; deterministic gradients and unbiased stochastic gradients are both admitted through the oracle symbol.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Exact diffusion is the three-stage recursion, for \(k\ge0\), \(\psi_i^{k+1}=w_i^k-\mu_i g_i(w_i^k;\xi_i^{k+1})\), \(\phi_i^{k+1}=\psi_i^{k+1}+w_i^k-\psi_i^k\), and \(w_i^{k+1}=\sum_{j=1}^n\bar a_{ji}\phi_j^{k+1}\), with an initialization such as \(\psi_i^0=w_i^0\). The middle equality is the exact-diffusion correction: it retains the increment between consecutive adapted states while adding the preceding primal state before combination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact diffusion is an adapt-correct-combine decentralized method. Each agent first takes a local gradient or sampled-gradient step, then forms a corrected state from the new adapted point, the current primal point, and the previous adapted point, and finally combines corrected states using the averaged network weights.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method is defined by the ordered adapt, correction, and combination equations with \(\bar A=(I+A)/2\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Stacking agent variables gives \(\Psi^{k+1}=W^k-MG(W^k;\xi^{k+1})\), \(\Phi^{k+1}=\Psi^{k+1}+W^k-\Psi^k\), and \(W^{k+1}=\bar A^\top\Phi^{k+1}\).
special_cases_latex: Setting \(g_i(w;\xi)=\nabla f_i(w)\) gives deterministic exact diffusion.
Using an unbiased sampled gradient gives stochastic exact diffusion.

knowledge_statements.title: Deterministic Exact Diffusion
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deterministic exact diffusion applies a local gradient step, a one-step bias correction, and neighbor averaging at every iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\) be a symmetric doubly stochastic mixing matrix and \(\bar A=(I+A)/2\). knowledge_statements.title: Disconnected Constraints Yield Only Componentwise Correction
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without a connected consensus operator, primal-dual correction enforces componentwise consensus and stationarity rather than the intended global problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \ker B\supsetneq\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1\}, then BX=0 permits distinct constants on different connected components. Moreover, G+B^{\mathsf T}Y=0 implies G\perp\ker B, imposing zero gradient sum on each component rather than only globally.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a connected consensus operator, a multiplier cancels heterogeneous local gradients exactly when they sum to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let B\in\mathbb R^{m\times n} satisfy \ker B=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1\}. For G\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}, \exists Y\in\mathbb R^{m\times d}:G+B^{\mathsf T}Y=0 if and only if \mathbf1^{\mathsf T}G=0.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier Gauge Freedom
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Redundant consensus constraints make the correction state nonunique without altering primal stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If Y satisfies G+B^{\mathsf T}Y=0, then Y+H satisfies it for every H\in\ker(B^{\mathsf T}). Thus the correction state is unique only modulo \ker(B^{\mathsf T}) unless a gauge or full-row-rank constraint representation is imposed.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Views of Exact Correction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consensus-constrained saddle representation of exact decentralized correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\in(\mathbb R^d)^n\), let \(F(X)=\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x_i)\), and choose a linear map \(B\) satisfying \(\ker B=\{\mathbf1\otimes x:x\in\mathbb R^d\}\). The decentralized problem is equivalently \[\min_X F(X)\quad\text{subject to}\quad BX=0,\] with Lagrangian \(L(X,Y)=F(X)+\langle Y,BX\rangle\) and optimality inclusion \[0\in \begin{pmatrix}\partial F&B^\top\\-B&0\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}X\\Y\end{pmatrix}.\] Exact-correction state variables can therefore be interpreted as transformed dual variables accumulating consensus-constraint violations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Consensus optimization is a linearly constrained problem whose dual variable accumulates disagreement; exact-correction memory can be viewed as a transformed dual state.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i:\mathbb R^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex.
\(\ker B\) equals the consensus subspace.
A saddle point of \(L\) exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Consensus optimality is equivalent to the displayed primal-dual monotone inclusion.

knowledge_statements.title: Naive Forward Treatment of Skew Consensus Coupling Is Expansive
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonzero skew consensus coupling cannot be used naively as the forward component of ordinary forward-backward splitting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \mathcal K be a nonzero bounded skew-adjoint linear operator. For every \gamma>0 and z, \|(I-\gamma\mathcal K)z\|^2=\|z\|^2+\gamma^2\|\mathcal Kz\|^2. Thus the forward map is expansive on every direction for which \mathcal Kz\ne0.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal K^*=-\mathcal K and \mathcal K\ne0.
\gamma>0.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal Kz\ne0\Longrightarrow\|(I-\gamma\mathcal K)z\|>\|z\|;\text{ a separate splitting or preconditioner analysis is required}.

knowledge_statements.title: Operator-Splitting Views of Exact Correction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone-inclusion and fixed-point representation of consensus correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the consensus-constrained convex problem, define on the primal-dual product space \[\mathcal A(X,Y)=(\partial F(X),0),\qquad \mathcal B(X,Y)=(B^\top Y,-BX).\] Then the optimality system is \(0\in(\mathcal A+\mathcal B)(X,Y)\). Whenever the chosen preconditioner \(P\) makes the relevant resolvents well defined, a splitting method generates a fixed-point iteration \[Z^{k+1}=T(Z^k),\qquad \operatorname{Fix}T=\operatorname{zer}(\mathcal A+\mathcal B).\] Eliminating or linearly transforming the dual component of such an iteration produces the two-step correction memory appearing in several exact decentralized primal recursions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact decentralized corrections can arise by splitting the primal-dual consensus inclusion and eliminating the dual state, leaving a two-step primal fixed-point iteration.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is proper, closed, and convex.
\(B\) is linear and its kernel is the consensus subspace.
The preconditioned splitting operator \(T\) is well defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Fix}T=\operatorname{zer}(\mathcal A+\mathcal B)\), and its primal fixed points solve consensus optimization.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without normalization, directed mixing can optimize a Perron-weighted objective instead of the intended uniform aggregate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let directed mixing have nonuniform stationary influence weights \(\pi_i>0\). knowledge_statements.title: Push-Pull Optimization Methods
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Agents use a row-stochastic operator for primal mixing and a column-stochastic operator for gradient tracking, thereby accommodating directed communication without a common doubly stochastic matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a stepsize \(\alpha>0\), initialize \(x_i^0\in\mathbb{R}^d\) and \(y_i^0=\nabla f_i(x_i^0)\). Stack the local variables as \(x^k\) and \(y^k\). The push-pull iteration is
\[
x^{k+1}=Rx^k-\alpha y^k,\qquad y^{k+1}=Cy^k+\nabla f(x^{k+1})-\nabla f(x^k),
\]
where the gradient map is applied blockwise. The row-stochastic operator forms primal averages, while the column-stochastic operator preserves the sum of tracking variables. Stop under a prescribed consensus-stationarity tolerance or budget and return the agent states.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}\) is differentiable.
The primal matrix \(R\) is row-stochastic and the tracking matrix \(C\) is column-stochastic.
All products and communicated entries are well defined on the directed graph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iteration couples row-stochastic primal mixing with column-stochastic tracking of the aggregate gradient.

knowledge_statements.title: Consensus Fixed-Point Boundary of Combine-Then-Proximal Updates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A consensual fixed point of plain constant-step proximal consensus must solve every local composite problem, which is stronger than solving their sum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For fixed \(\alpha>0\) and row-stochastic \(W\), a consensual state \(x_i=x^*\) is a fixed point of the accepted update exactly when, for every agent,
\[
x^*=\operatorname{prox}_{\alpha r_i}(x^*-\alpha\nabla f_i(x^*))
\iff0\in\nabla f_i(x^*)+\partial r_i(x^*).
\]
Aggregate stationarity does not generally imply these agentwise conditions.
assumptions_latex: The accepted combine-then-proximal recursion uses fixed \(\alpha>0\).
\(W\) is row-stochastic.
Each \(r_i\) is proper, closed, and convex, and each \(f_i\) is differentiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbf1\otimes x^*\text{ is fixed}\iff0\in\nabla f_i(x^*)+\partial r_i(x^*)\ \forall i.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact obstruction to aggregate optimality for the accepted uncorrected constant-step recursion.

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal Consensus Methods
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each agent averages neighboring iterates, takes a local gradient step, and applies its local proximal map to handle nonsmooth structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize \(x_i^0\in\mathbb{R}^d\). At iteration \(k\), agent \(i\) forms the consensus point \(v_i^k=\sum_jw_{ij}x_j^k\), obtains \(g_i^k=\nabla f_i(v_i^k)\), and computes
\[
x_i^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\alpha_k r_i}\!\left(v_i^k-\alpha_k g_i^k\right),
\qquad
\operatorname{prox}_{\alpha r}(u)=\mathop{\arg\min}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^d}\left\{r(x)+\frac{\lVert x-u\rVert^2}{2\alpha}\right\}.
\]
Agents exchange the new iterates and repeat. Stop under a prescribed consensus-optimality residual or budget and return the local states.
assumptions_latex: Each agent has a proper closed convex proximable function \(r_i\) and a convex differentiable function \(f_i\).
The mixing matrix \(W=[w_{ij}]\) is nonnegative and row-stochastic.
The stepsize \(\alpha_k>0\) is prescribed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each new local iterate is a proximal correction of a consensus-mixed point using local first-order information.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basic combine-then-proximal-gradient consensus scheme for composite convex objectives.

knowledge_statements.title: Tracker-Initialization Bias in Proximal Gradient Tracking
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Incorrect tracker initialization creates a permanent aggregate offset and shifts the fixed-point stationarity condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For doubly stochastic mixing and the gradient-difference tracker recursion, define
\[
\delta=\sum_i y_i^0-\sum_i\nabla f_i(x_i^0).
\]
Then
\[
\sum_i y_i^k-\sum_i\nabla f_i(x_i^k)=\delta
\]
for every \(k\). At a consensual fixed point with tracker consensus, the proximal condition is therefore shifted to
\[
0\in\nabla F(x^*)+{\delta\over n}+\partial r(x^*),
\]
so true composite stationarity is not guaranteed unless \(\delta=0\).
assumptions_latex: The tracker update uses doubly stochastic mixing and gradient differences.
A consensual fixed point with tracker consensus exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \delta\ne0\Longrightarrow\text{the fixed-point condition is generally }0\in\nabla F(x^*)+\delta/n+\partial r(x^*).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistent aggregate offset caused by incorrect tracker initialization.

knowledge_statements.title: Consensual Fixed Points Are Composite Stationary
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any consensual fixed point of correctly initialized proximal gradient tracking is stationary for the aggregate smooth objective plus the common regularizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F=n^{-1}\sum_i f_i\). Suppose the fixed mixing matrix \(W\) is doubly stochastic with \(\ker(I-W)=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1\}\), the tracker invariant \(\sum_i y_i=\sum_i\nabla f_i(x_i)\) holds, and the displayed proximal gradient-tracking recursion has a fixed point with \(x_i=x^*\) for every \(i\). The tracker fixed-point equation then makes all \(y_i\) equal to \(\nabla F(x^*)\), and
\[
x^*=\operatorname{prox}_{\alpha r}(x^*-\alpha y_i)
\iff0\in\nabla F(x^*)+\partial r(x^*).
\]
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i\) is differentiable and \(r\) is proper, closed, and convex.
\(W\) is doubly stochastic and has only consensus fixed vectors.
The tracker-sum invariant and the fixed-point equations of the common-regularizer recursion hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_i=x^*\ \forall i\text{ at a fixed point}\Longrightarrow0\in\nabla F(x^*)+\partial r(x^*).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactness property of a correctly initialized common-regularizer proximal gradient-tracking recursion.

abla f_i(x_i^{k+1})-
abla f_i(x_i^k),\qquad y_i^0=
abla f_i(x_i^0),\] where \(\alpha_k>0\) and \(\operatorname{prox}_{\alpha r}(v)=\arg\min_u\{r(u)+(2\alpha)^{-1}\|u-v\|^2\}\). The defining feature is the simultaneous proximal composite update and gradient-increment tracking recursion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each agent mixes neighboring primal states, subtracts a local estimate of the network-average gradient, applies the proximal map of the common nonsmooth term, and updates that gradient estimate by mixing old trackers and adding its own gradient increment. knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be closed and convex. Agent \(i\) holds a convex function \(f_i:X\to\mathbb R\). Let \(h:X\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable and strictly convex on the relevant domain, with Bregman divergence \(D_h(x,z)=h(x)-h(z)-\langle\nabla h(z),x-z\rangle\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional distributed convex optimization in a common non-Euclidean geometry; stochastic subgradients and time-varying mixing are allowed at the definitional level.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A distributed non-Euclidean descent method is a network iteration in which each agent forms a mixed reference point \(v_i^k\in X\), commonly \(v_i^k=\sum_j w_{ij}^k x_j^k\), chooses \(g_i^k\in\partial f_i(v_i^k)\), and sets \[x_i^{k+1}\in\arg\min_{x\in X}\left\{\alpha_k\langle g_i^k,x\rangle+D_h(x,v_i^k)\right\},\qquad \alpha_k>0.\] More generally, the linear term may contain a locally available unbiased stochastic subgradient. Membership in the family requires that communication supplies the reference or dual-coordinate aggregation and that the local descent step is regularized by \(D_h\), rather than necessarily by squared Euclidean distance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Agents communicate to form local reference points and then minimize a first-order model of their local objective plus a Bregman divergence from the reference point. The divergence, generated by a strictly convex distance-generating function, determines the non-Euclidean geometry.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The family is characterized by a network-generated reference \(v_i^k\) and a Bregman-regularized local first-order update for every agent and iteration.
equivalent_formulations_latex: When the minimizer lies in the relative interior and no constraint normal is active, optimality is equivalent to \(\nabla h(x_i^{k+1})=\nabla h(v_i^k)-\alpha_k g_i^k\).
special_cases_latex: For \(h(x)=\tfrac12\|x\|_2^2\), the update is projected distributed subgradient descent.
On the probability simplex with negative entropy as \(h\), the local step is an exponentiated-gradient or multiplicative-weights update.
immediate_consequences_latex: Changing \(h\) changes the local geometry while leaving the separable first-order model and communication layer conceptually distinct.

Objective–Disagreement Decomposition
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Aggregate suboptimality is bounded by averaged local first-order terms plus a disagreement penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F=n^{-1}\sum_i f_i\), \(g_i\in\partial f_i(x_i)\), and \(\bar x=n^{-1}\sum_i x_i\). If every \(f_i\) is convex and \(G\)-Lipschitz on \(X\), then for every \(x\in X\),
\[
F(\bar x)-F(x)\le {1\over n}\sum_i\langle g_i,x_i-x\rangle+{G\over n}\sum_i\|x_i-\bar x\|.
\]
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i\) is convex and \(G\)-Lipschitz on \(X\).
\(g_i\in\partial f_i(x_i)\), and \(x,x_i,\bar x\in X\).

\alpha_k\langle g_i^k,x_i^{k+1}-x\rangle\le D_h(x,v_i^k)-D_h(x,x_i^{k+1})-D_h(x_i^{k+1},v_i^k).
\]

\(h\) is differentiable and strongly convex on the relevant domain.
The displayed minimizer exists, \(\alpha_k>0\), and \(g_i^k\) is finite.

knowledge_statements.title: Bregman Proximal Map and Optimality Condition
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Bregman proximal point uniquely minimizes a convex function plus a Bregman distance and is characterized by a normal-cone inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\alpha>0\), define
\[
P_{\alpha\phi}^{h,X}(v)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\{\alpha\phi(x)+D_h(x,v)\},\qquad D_h(x,v)=h(x)-h(v)-\langle\nabla h(v),x-v\rangle.
\]
If the minimum is attained and the convex subdifferential sum rule applies, strong convexity of \(h\) makes the minimizer unique, and
\[
x^+=P_{\alpha\phi}^{h,X}(v)\iff0\in\alpha\partial\phi(x^+)+\nabla h(x^+)-\nabla h(v)+N_X(x^+).
\]
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(\phi\) is proper, closed, and convex.
\(h\) is differentiable and strongly convex on the relevant domain.
The minimum is attained and a standard convex subdifferential sum qualification holds.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local Bregman proximal operation underlying distributed implementations; no network recursion is selected.

\]

knowledge_statements.title: Mirror-Map Scaling Invariance
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive rescaling changes Bregman distance and curvature equally, leaving the standard geometry score unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(\widetilde h=ch\) for \(c>0\), then \(D_{\widetilde h}=cD_h\) and \(\widetilde h\) is \(c\mu\)-strongly convex whenever \(h\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex. Hence
\[
{G^2D_{\widetilde h}(x^*,x^0)\over c\mu}={G^2D_h(x^*,x^0)\over\mu}.
\]
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex in the selected norm.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rules out artificial improvement of the geometry-selection score by scalar rescaling.

knowledge_statements.title: Canonical Euclidean and Entropic Geometries
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Squared Euclidean and negative-entropy geometries provide canonical norm-divergence pairings for Euclidean domains and probability simplices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For Euclidean geometry, \(h(x)=\tfrac12\|x\|_2^2\) is one-strongly convex in \(\|\cdot\|_2\) and \(D_h(x,y)=\tfrac12\|x-y\|_2^2\). On the simplex \(\Delta_d\), negative entropy \(h(x)=\sum_jx_j\log x_j\) is one-strongly convex in \(\|\cdot\|_1\); for \(y\) with positive coordinates,
\[
D_h(x,y)=\sum_jx_j\log(x_j/y_j),
\]
and at \(u=\mathbf1/d\), \(\sup_{x\in\Delta_d}D_h(x,u)=\log d\). Entropic geometry therefore pairs a logarithmic simplex Bregman radius with the dual norm \(\|\cdot\|_\infty\).
assumptions_latex: For entropy geometry, the second argument has strictly positive coordinates.
The convention \(0\log0=0\) is used.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical choices illustrating feasible-set, primal-norm, dual-norm, and Bregman-radius matching.

knowledge_statements.title: Mirror-Geometry Selection
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose the norm and mirror map together to reduce the product of squared dual-gradient scale and Bregman distance relative to strong convexity, while retaining tractable distributed updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a positive integer \(T\), constant stepsize \(\alpha>0\), and the standard weighted or averaged mirror-descent output, the optimization bound has the form
\[
\frac{D_h(x^*,x^0)}{\alpha T}+\frac{\alpha G^2}{2\mu}.
\]
Balancing these terms gives
\[
\alpha=\sqrt{\frac{2\mu D_h(x^*,x^0)}{G^2T}}.
\]
Thus a mirror geometry should be selected jointly with its norm to control the Bregman distance to an optimizer, the dual-norm scale of admissible subgradients, and the strong-convexity modulus. In a distributed implementation, mirror-coordinate aggregation and local mirror or proximal subproblems should also remain computationally tractable.
assumptions_latex: The objective \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) is convex, \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) is nonempty and convex, and \(x^*\in\mathop{\arg\min}_{x\in X}f(x)\).
Every employed subgradient satisfies \(\lVert g\rVert_*\leq G\) with respect to the dual of the selected norm \(\lVert\cdot\rVert\).
The selected differentiable mirror map \(h\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex with respect to \(\lVert\cdot\rVert\), and \(D_h(x^*,x^0)\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Within a candidate family of mirror geometries, the standard bound favors choices jointly controlling \(G^2D_h(x^*,x^0)/\mu\) while keeping mirror and proximal operations tractable.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometry-selection principle derived from the standard convex mirror-descent bound.

knowledge_statements.title: Bregman Divergence Is Not a Metric
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bregman divergence is a directed discrepancy, so metric consensus arguments do not transfer automatically.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Although \(D_h(x,y)=h(x)-h(y)-\langle\nabla h(y),x-y\rangle\ge0\), it is generally asymmetric and need not satisfy the triangle inequality. For \(h(t)=t\log t\), \(D_h(1,2)=1-\log2\ne2\log2-1=D_h(2,1)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Bregman-Geometry Boundaries
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Entropy mirror coordinates are undefined at zero coordinates, and ordinary convex averaging generally differs from averaging in mirror coordinates and mapping back.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the entropy generator \(h(x)=\sum_{\ell=1}^d x_\ell\log x_\ell\), the mirror coordinate satisfies \(\nabla h(x)=\mathbf{1}+\log x\) on the positive orthant and is not finite when a coordinate of \(x\) is zero. Consequently, an iterate or communicated center on the boundary makes a gradient-based mirror update undefined unless a suitable extension or limiting convention is specified. Moreover, because \(\nabla h\) is nonlinear, the primal average \(\sum_jw_{ij}x_j\) generally differs from the mirror-coordinate barycenter
\[
(\nabla h)^{-1}\!\left(\sum_jw_{ij}\nabla h(x_j)\right),
\]
whenever the inverse is defined. Thus replacing mirror-coordinate aggregation by ordinary primal consensus generally changes the intended Bregman geometry.
assumptions_latex: The entropy generator is \(h(x)=\sum_{\ell=1}^d x_\ell\log x_\ell\) on the nonnegative orthant, with gradient defined on its positive interior.
For each agent \(i\), the mixing coefficients satisfy \(w_{ij}\geq0\) and \(\sum_jw_{ij}=1\).
Whenever a mirror-coordinate barycenter is invoked, \(\sum_jw_{ij}\nabla h(x_j)\) lies in the range of \(\nabla h\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Boundary points can make entropy mirror coordinates undefined, and primal averaging generally differs from averaging in mirror coordinates followed by the inverse mirror map.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Corrected-Surrogate Fixed-Point Certificate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With exact correction for the other agents' gradients, a surrogate best-response fixed point is exactly a composite stationary point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Phi(x)=\sum_jf_j(x)+r(x)\) on \(X\), and define
\[
\widehat x_i(z)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\left\{\widetilde f_i(x;z)+\left\langle\sum_{j\ne i}\nabla f_j(z),x-z\right\rangle+r(x)\right\}.
\]
If the surrogate is differentiable, strongly convex, and first-order consistent, and the convex sum rule applies, then
\[
z=\widehat x_i(z)\iff0\in\sum_j\nabla f_j(z)+\partial r(z)+N_X(z).
\]
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_j\) is differentiable.
\(r\) is proper, closed, and convex; \(X\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(\widetilde f_i(\cdot;z)\) is differentiable, strongly convex, and first-order consistent.
A standard convex subdifferential sum qualification holds.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stationarity certificate using an exact aggregate-gradient correction, independent of its network implementation.

knowledge_statements.title: First-Order-Consistent Strongly Convex Surrogate

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A surrogate \(\widetilde f_i(\cdot;z)\) is admissible when it is strongly convex on \(X\), its gradient is continuous in the relevant arguments, and
\[
\nabla_x\widetilde f_i(z;z)=\nabla f_i(z).
\]
Global majorization \(\widetilde f_i(x;z)\ge f_i(x)\) is an additional variant-specific condition and does not follow from first-order consistency.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is convex.
\(f_i\) is differentiable on the relevant domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widetilde f_i(\cdot;z)\text{ is strongly convex},\qquad\nabla_x\widetilde f_i(z;z)=\nabla f_i(z).

\]

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F(x)=\sum_i f_i(x)+r(x)\) over a closed convex set \(X\), agent \(i\) constructs at \(x_i^k\) a strongly convex surrogate \(\widetilde f_i(\cdot;x_i^k)\) satisfying value-gradient consistency there. knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A distributed curvature method is a network algorithm whose local search direction \(d_i^k\) is determined by a second-order model \[d_i^k\in\arg\min_{d\in\mathbb R^d}\left\{\langle g_i^k,d\rangle+\tfrac12\langle d,B_i^k d\rangle\right\},\] or by a regularized version with \(B_i^k+\mu_k I\succ0\), and whose state update combines \(x_i^k+\alpha_k d_i^k\) with information received from neighbors. knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Membership requires an iteratively generated matrix-valued curvature model that determines the local direction and a communication step coupling agents' states or curvature information.

special_cases_latex: Choosing \(B_i^k=\nabla^2 f_i(x_i^k)+\mu_kI\) gives a regularized local Newton method.

\[
\|\widehat p-p\|\le\frac{\rho+\varepsilon_g+\varepsilon_H\|p\|}{\mu-\varepsilon_H}.
\]

\(\|\widehat H-H\|\le\varepsilon_H<\mu\).

knowledge_statements.title: Absolute and Relative Hessian Heterogeneity

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H_i(x)=\nabla^2f_i(x)\) and \(\bar H(x)=n^{-1}\sum_iH_i(x)\). Define \(\delta_H=\sup_{x\in\mathcal D}\max_i\|H_i(x)-\bar H(x)\|_2\). When \(\bar H(x)\succ0\), a relative regime satisfies \(\|H_i(x)-\bar H(x)\|_2\le\eta\lambda_{\min}(\bar H(x))\). If \(\eta<1\), then \((1-\eta)\bar H(x)\preceq H_i(x)\preceq(1+\eta)\bar H(x)\).

The relative regime assumes \(\bar H(x)\succ0\) throughout \(\mathcal D\).

A family indexed by a parameter is asymptotically homogeneous when its corresponding modulus converges to zero.

knowledge_statements.title: Stationarity Does Not Certify Global Optimality
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero aggregate gradient can identify a local maximum rather than a global minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If every agent has \(f_i(x)=(x^2-1)^2\), then \(F(x)=(x^2-1)^2\). The consensual state \(x_i=0\) satisfies \(\nabla F(0)=0\), but
\[
F(0)=1>0=F(1)=F(-1),
\]
and \(0\) is a strict local maximum.

knowledge_statements.title: Consensus First-Order Stationarity for Smooth Nonconvex Networks
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The generic smooth nonconvex target is consensus plus a small aggregate gradient, not global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(F(x)=n^{-1}\sum_i f_i(x)\), a product state is consensual first-order stationary when
\[
x_1=\cdots=x_n=x^*,\qquad\nabla F(x^*)=0.
\]
It is \((\varepsilon_c,\varepsilon_s)\)-approximately stationary when
\[
{1\over n}\sum_i\|x_i-\bar x\|\le\varepsilon_c,\qquad\|\nabla F(\bar x)\|\le\varepsilon_s.
\]
assumptions_latex: Every \(f_i\) is differentiable.

knowledge_statements.title: Consensus-Based Dual Decomposition
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each agent maintains a local price, solves its own Lagrangian subproblem, then mixes prices with neighbors while adding its local coupling residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let there be \(n\geq1\) agents. For each \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\), let \(X_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{d_i}\), \(f_i:X_i\to\mathbb R\), \(A_i:\mathbb R^{d_i}\to\mathbb R^m\), and \(b_i\in\mathbb R^m\), with \(\sum_{i=1}^n b_i=b\). Let \(\Lambda\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) be a nonempty closed convex multiplier set, and initialize \(\lambda_i^0\in\Lambda\). At iteration \(k\), agent \(i\) computes \[x_i^k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x_i\in X_i}\bigl(f_i(x_i)+(\lambda_i^k)^\top(A_ix_i-b_i)\bigr),\] exchanges multiplier copies with its neighbors, and updates \[\lambda_i^{k+1}=\Pi_\Lambda\!\left(\sum_{j=1}^n w_{ij}^k\lambda_j^k+\alpha_k(A_ix_i^k-b_i)\right).\] Stop when neighboring multiplier copies agree within a prescribed tolerance and the aggregate residual \(\left\lVert\sum_{i=1}^n(A_ix_i^k-b_i)\right\rVert\) is small. Return the common price estimate together with an ergodically recovered primal allocation.
assumptions_latex: For every iterate, each local Lagrangian subproblem attains a minimum.
The local dual supergradients are uniformly bounded on the nonempty closed convex multiplier set \(\Lambda\).
Each \(W^k\) is doubly stochastic, the mixing sequence is uniformly connected, and its positive weights satisfy the method's required uniform lower bound.

knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Primal Recovery
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted averages of local primal responses provide a recoverable decision; its coupling residual and primal–dual gap certify feasibility and, when feasible, suboptimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For dual-decomposition iterates \(x_i^t\) and positive weights \(\alpha_t\), define \(S_k=\sum_{t=0}^k\alpha_t\) and \[\bar x_i^k=S_k^{-1}\sum_{t=0}^k\alpha_tx_i^t.\] Agents can average their local residuals to evaluate \(r^k=\sum_iA_i\bar x_i^k-b\). \(q(\lambda^k)\) is a valid dual lower bound.
Agents can aggregate the local residuals and objective values.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Feasibility-Preserving Allocation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from a balanced allocation, agents exchange marginal costs and move resources along graph edges; the Laplacian update preserves total resource exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For scalar allocations, solve \(\min_x\sum_i f_i(x_i)\) subject to \(\mathbf1^\top x=d\). Choose a feasible initialization \(x^0\) with \(\mathbf1^\top x^0=d\), and let \(L_G\) be the Laplacian of a connected undirected communication graph. Iterate \[x^{k+1}=x^k-\alpha_kL_G\nabla f(x^k).\] Equivalently, each agent exchanges marginal costs and applies \(x_i^{k+1}=x_i^k-\alpha_k\sum_ja_{ij}(f_i'(x_i^k)-f_j'(x_j^k))\). Stop when neighboring marginal costs agree within tolerance; output \(x^k\). Since \(\mathbf1^\top L_G=0\), every iterate satisfies the resource balance exactly.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) is differentiable.
The communication graph is connected, undirected, and has nonnegative symmetric edge weights.
The initial allocation satisfies \(\mathbf1^\top x^0=d\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Laplacian-gradient allocation preserving an equality resource balance at every iteration.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The Laplacian identity does establish exact preservation of the initial resource balance, but the cited general decentralized-consensus locator is not specific enough to support this marginal-cost resource-allocation algorithm or its stopping criterion.
