knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Resource Allocation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Allocations descend on local Lagrangians while price copies mix and integrate local imbalance, jointly seeking stationarity, price consensus, and resource balance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min_{x_i\in X_i}\sum_if_i(x_i)\) subject to \(\sum_ix_i=d\), select shares \(d_i\) with \(\sum_id_i=d\), initialize \(x_i^0\in X_i\) and local prices \(\lambda_i^0\). With a mixing matrix \(W=(w_{ij})\), perform \[x_i^{k+1}=P_{X_i}\!\left(x_i^k-\alpha_k(\nabla f_i(x_i^k)+\lambda_i^k)\right),\] \[\lambda_i^{k+1}=\sum_jw_{ij}\lambda_j^k+\beta_k(x_i^{k+1}-d_i).\] Stop when primal changes, price disagreement, and the aggregate balance residual are below tolerances. Output \((x_i^k,\lambda_i^k)\); at a fixed point, allocations satisfy local stationarity and prices agree.
assumptions_latex: Each \(X_i\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and each \(f_i\) is convex and differentiable.
The communication graph is connected and \(W\) is doubly stochastic.
Stepsizes are chosen to satisfy the stability conditions of the selected primal-dual discretization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any converged fixed point with zero aggregate residual satisfies the KKT conditions for the convex resource-allocation problem.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected primal descent coupled to distributed price consensus and balance innovations.

Conversely, zero aggregate residual at an arbitrary fixed point does not imply price consensus. Thus the stated fixed-point and KKT conclusion is not justified; an exact sourced primal-dual discretization is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Saddle-Point Dynamics
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal variables descend the network Lagrangian while edge multipliers ascend it; Euler discretization yields a local-message primal-dual iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The continuous-time network saddle dynamics for \(L\) are
\[
\dot x(t)=-\nabla_xL(x(t),y(t))=-\nabla f(x(t))-B^\top y(t),\qquad \dot y(t)=\nabla_yL(x(t),y(t))=Bx(t).
\]
Given \((x^0,y^0)\), the forward-Euler realization is
\[
x^{k+1}=x^k-h\bigl(\nabla f(x^k)+B^\top y^k\bigr),\qquad y^{k+1}=y^k+hBx^k.
\]
Each derivative or update uses local gradients and incident-edge communication. A continuous trajectory is reported at a prescribed horizon; the discrete method stops at a horizon or when its consensus and stationarity residuals satisfy selected tolerances.
assumptions_latex: The graph incidence matrix is \(B\), and \(f\) is convex and continuously differentiable.
A saddle point of \(L(x,y)=f(x)+\langle y,Bx\rangle\) exists.
For the displayed Euler discretization, a step size \(h>0\) is chosen for the desired stability regime.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Equilibria of the flow, and fixed points of its Euler discretization, are precisely primal-dual solutions satisfying \(Bx=0\) and \(\nabla f(x)+B^\top y=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained smooth convex consensus saddle flow and its forward-Euler discretization.

children.title: Distributed Predictive-Corrective Method Family
children.top_down_role: Predictive and corrective methods for network saddle problems.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(Z=\prod_i Z_i\) be a finite-dimensional product Hilbert space and consider \(0\in A z+Bz\), where \(A\) is maximally monotone and block-separable and \(B\) is monotone, Lipschitz, and graph-local. Let \(J_{\gamma A}=(I+\gamma A)^{-1}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic synchronous predictor-corrector splittings for monotone network saddle inclusions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A distributed predictive-corrective method is an iteration with a predicted state and a corrected state, \[p^k=J_{\gamma_k A}(z^k-\gamma_k Bz^k),\qquad z^{k+1}=p^k-\gamma_k(Bp^k-Bz^k),\] or a metrically equivalent block form. It is distributed when \(J_{\gamma_k A}\) decomposes into local resolvents and each block \((Bz)_i\) can be evaluated from agent \(i\)'s data and current neighbor states. The first line predicts a proximal primal-dual state from one network evaluation; the second corrects it using the change of the coupled saddle operator between \(z^k\) and \(p^k\). A fixed point obeys \(p^\star=z^\star\) and hence \(0\in Az^\star+Bz^\star\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method first predicts a local proximal primal-dual state using the coupled operator at the current network state. It then corrects the prediction using the difference between coupled-operator evaluations at the prediction and the old state. Local resolvents and neighbor-only coupled evaluations make the scheme distributed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The predictive-corrective family consists of graph-local two-evaluation splittings whose fixed points solve \(0\in A+B\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The displayed update is the forward-backward-forward fixed-point map \(T_\gamma z=p-\gamma(Bp-Bz)\), where \(p=J_{\gamma A}(z-\gamma Bz)\).
special_cases_latex: When \(A=N_C\), the prediction is a projection onto \(C\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(z^\star=T_\gamma z^\star\), then \(z^\star=J_{\gamma A}(z^\star-\gamma Bz^\star)\) and therefore \(0\in Az^\star+Bz^\star\).
boundary_notes: The definition does not assert convergence or prescribe a Lipschitz-dependent stepsize.
Methods using a single forward evaluation belong instead to the forward-backward subclass.

notation.meaning: Resolvent of the monotone operator A.

review_flags: A precise inspected source for the distributed specialization is required.
knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Predictive-Corrective Primal-Dual Method
Distributed Extragradient Methods
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mix neighboring iterates, predict with one operator evaluation, and correct from the same mixed base using an evaluation at the predictor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize \(z^0\in K\) and choose \(\alpha>0\). At iteration \(k\), compute the distributed predictor and corrector
\[
u^k=\Pi_K\!\left(\mathcal Wz^k-\alpha F(z^k)\right),\qquad z^{k+1}=\Pi_K\!\left(\mathcal Wz^k-\alpha F(u^k)\right).
\]
Each block of \(\mathcal Wz\) is obtained from neighbor messages, and each block of \(F\) is evaluated locally. The second evaluation at \(u^k\) corrects the first-order step without an implicit solve. Stop when a prescribed network variational-inequality residual and the disagreement \(\lVert (I-\mathcal W)z^k\rVert\) are below tolerance; output \(z^k\) or an ergodic average.
assumptions_latex: The closed convex set \(K=K_1\times\cdots\times K_n\) is nonempty.
The block operator \(F:K\to\mathbb{R}^{nd}\) is monotone and Lipschitz.
The mixing matrix \(W\) respects a connected graph and is doubly stochastic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any fixed point lying in consensus solves the variational inequality \(\langle F(z^\star),z-z^\star\rangle\ge0\) for every consensus-feasible \(z\in K\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous projected extragradient with one mixing operation at each evaluation stage.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The cited locators do not specifically support this two-mixing projected distributed extragradient formula or establish that it solves the intended network saddle problem. Plain mixing without a consensus constraint, tracking variable, or correction mechanism can converge to a problem different from the aggregate variational inequality.

knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Optimistic Methods
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An optimistic method predicts the next operator value by extrapolating the two latest evaluations, then combines this correction with neighbor mixing and projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose \(z^{-1}=z^0\in K\) and \(\alpha>0\). For \(k=0,1,\ldots\), each agent exchanges its current block, evaluates its local operator block, and performs
\[
q^k=2F(z^k)-F(z^{k-1}),\qquad z^{k+1}=\Pi_K\!\left(\mathcal Wz^k-\alpha q^k\right).
\]
The stored value \(F(z^{k-1})\) makes the iteration a one-new-evaluation predictive correction. Stop when both \(\lVert z^{k+1}-z^k\rVert\) and \(\lVert(I-\mathcal W)z^k\rVert\) meet prescribed tolerances, or after a fixed horizon; output the final or averaged iterate according to the convergence guarantee being used.
assumptions_latex: The closed convex set \(K\) is a Cartesian product across agents.
The operator \(F\) is monotone and Lipschitz on \(K\).
The matrix \(W\) is graph-compatible and doubly stochastic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A consensual fixed point satisfies the network variational inequality, while the correction \(2F(z^k)-F(z^{k-1})\) uses one new operator evaluation per iteration after initialization.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected one-call optimistic method with synchronous graph mixing.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The cited material does not specifically support the displayed distributed optimistic iteration. A one-call optimistic operator step combined only with mixing generally needs additional structural assumptions or tracking machinery to represent the intended aggregate network problem.

knowledge_statements.title: Predictive–Corrective Relations
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Along a consistent small-step trajectory, extragradient evaluation and optimistic extrapolation approximate the same future operator value to first order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Taylor expansion at \(z^k\) gives the extragradient evaluation
\[
F(u^k)=F(z^k)-\alpha JF(z^k)F(z^k)+O(\alpha^2).
\]
The displacement assumption gives
\[
F(z^{k-1})=F(z^k)+\alpha JF(z^k)F(z^k)+O(\alpha^2),
\]
and therefore
\[
2F(z^k)-F(z^{k-1})=F(z^k)-\alpha JF(z^k)F(z^k)+O(\alpha^2)=F(u^k)+O(\alpha^2).
\]
Thus the extragradient evaluation at a predicted point and the optimistic extrapolation from stored evaluations implement locally matching predictive-corrective information through first order.
assumptions_latex: The operator \(F\) is twice continuously differentiable near \(z^k\), with locally bounded second derivative.
The recent displacement satisfies \(z^k-z^{k-1}=-\alpha F(z^k)+O(\alpha^2)\).
Projection and network-mixing errors are absent or themselves \(O(\alpha^2)\) in the local comparison.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Extragradient and optimistic corrections evaluate the same first-order prediction of the future operator, differing by \(O(\alpha^2)\) under the stated local trajectory relation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local first-order relation; it does not assert exact trajectory equivalence.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The local asymptotic relation is plausible under the stated trajectory assumption, but the cited general splitting section does not specifically support it. The statement also presents a derivation rather than a proof-free knowledge statement.

knowledge_statements.title: Network Saddle Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A standard network saddle regime combines connected doubly stochastic mixing, a positive consensus gap, and a monotone Lipschitz saddle operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A static network saddle regime is admissible when
\[
W\mathbf 1=\mathbf 1,\qquad \mathbf 1^\top W=\mathbf 1^\top,\qquad W_{ij}=0\ \text{for nonedges},\qquad \rho=\lVert W-J\rVert_2<1,
\]
and the stacked saddle operator \(F\) satisfies, for all domain points \(z,z'\),
\[
\langle F(z)-F(z'),z-z'\rangle\ge0,\qquad \lVert F(z)-F(z')\rVert\le L\lVert z-z'\rVert.
\]
Here \(\rho<1\) makes disagreement contract under mixing, while monotonicity and Lipschitz continuity specify the operator regime addressed by distributed extragradient or optimistic corrections.
assumptions_latex: The matrix \(W\) is nonnegative, graph-compatible, and doubly stochastic.
The fixed-point space satisfies \(\ker(I-W)=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf 1\}\).
Each local saddle operator is monotone and \(L\)-Lipschitz on the common domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pair \((L,\delta)\) separates operator difficulty from network difficulty; predictive-corrective step restrictions and rates may depend on both quantities.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Static connected-network regime for monotone Lipschitz saddle operators.

children.title: Distributed Augmentation-Splitting Method Family
children.top_down_role: Penalty-enhanced decompositions for consensus and general coupling.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min_{x\in X}\sum_i f_i(x_i)\) subject to \(Ax=b\), with block-sparse \(A\) conforming to a communication graph. For \(\rho>0\), define \(\mathcal L_\rho(x,y)=\sum_i f_i(x_i)+\langle y,Ax-b\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\|Ax-b\|^2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional equality-coupled optimization using augmented-Lagrangian penalties and decomposable block updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A distributed augmentation-splitting method is an iteration obtained by splitting the saddle optimality system of \(\mathcal L_\rho\) into locally solvable primal blocks and graph-local multiplier blocks. In a representative block form, \[x_i^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{u_i\in X_i}\mathcal L_\rho(x_1^{k+1},\ldots,x_{i-1}^{k+1},u_i,x_{i+1}^k,\ldots;x^k,y^k)+r_i^k(u_i),\] followed by \[y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho(Ax^{k+1}-b),\] where \(r_i^k\) is an optional local proximal regularizer. The defining features are a positive quadratic penalty on coupling violation, alternating or otherwise split primal processing, and multiplier ascent. Distribution requires each block to access only the rows of \(A\), residual components, and neighboring variables incident to it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This family augments an equality-constrained Lagrangian with a quadratic coupling penalty, splits the primal minimization into local blocks, and updates multipliers from the coupling residual. The method is distributed when the coupling matrix is graph sparse and every block update uses only incident residuals and neighbor variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An iteration belongs to this family when its local split steps act on the augmented Lagrangian and its dual step accumulates the graph-local feasibility residual \(Ax-b\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The quadratic term may be written \(\frac12\|Ax-b\|_R^2\) for a positive definite or semidefinite graph-local penalty metric \(R\).
special_cases_latex: Consensus ADMM results when \(Ax=b\) encodes equality of replicated variables.
immediate_consequences_latex: At any fixed point with unchanged multiplier, \(Ax^\star=b\).
boundary_notes: A pure dual-decomposition method with \(\rho=0\) is not augmentation-based.
Multi-block update order and regularization materially affect convergence but are not fixed by this definition.
review_flags: The supplied augmented-Lagrangian hint was not inspected at a statement-level locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Consensus ADMM
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Consensus ADMM alternates parallel local proximal solves, averaging into a shared variable, and scaled-dual updates enforcing agreement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Rewrite \(\min_z\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(z)\) as \(\min_{x,z}\sum_i f_i(x_i)\) subject to \(x_i=z\). Initialize \(z^0\) and \(u_i^0\). Scaled ADMM performs, in parallel,
\[
x_i^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{f_i/\rho}(z^k-u_i^k),
\]
followed by
\[
z^{k+1}=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n(x_i^{k+1}+u_i^k),\qquad u_i^{k+1}=u_i^k+x_i^{k+1}-z^{k+1}.
\]
Stop when the primal residuals \(x_i^k-z^k\) and dual residual \(\rho(z^k-z^{k-1})\) satisfy prescribed tolerances; output \(z^k\).
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i:\mathbb{R}^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex.
The consensus problem has a primal-dual solution.
The penalty parameter satisfies \(\rho>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every fixed point satisfies \(x_i^\star=z^\star\) for all \(i\) and the optimality conditions for \(\min_z\sum_i f_i(z)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scaled two-block ADMM for a centralized replicated-variable consensus model.

notation.meaning: Agent replicas and shared consensus variable

knowledge_statements.title: Edge-Based ADMM
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Edge-based ADMM gives each edge a coupling variable, alternates local node solves with edge averaging, and updates one multiplier per incidence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Represent consensus by \(x_i=z_e\) for every incidence \(i\in e\). Given \((z^0,u^0)\), scaled ADMM performs
\[
x_i^{k+1}=\arg\min_x\left\{f_i(x)+\frac\rho2\sum_{e\in E_i}\lVert x-z_e^k+u_{ie}^k\rVert^2\right\},
\]
then, for each edge \(e=\{i,j\}\),
\[
z_e^{k+1}=\frac{x_i^{k+1}+u_{ie}^k+x_j^{k+1}+u_{je}^k}{2},\qquad u_{ie}^{k+1}=u_{ie}^k+x_i^{k+1}-z_e^{k+1}.
\]
The analogous multiplier update is made for \((j,e)\). Stop when all incidence primal and dual residuals meet tolerance; output the node variables.
assumptions_latex: The undirected communication graph is connected.
Every local objective \(f_i\) is proper, closed, and convex.
The edge penalty satisfies \(\rho>0\), and a primal-dual solution exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At a fixed point, every incidence constraint holds; graph connectivity then implies \(x_1=\cdots=x_n\), and the common value minimizes \(\sum_i f_i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scaled ADMM on node-edge incidence constraints for an undirected graph.

children.title: Regularized Distributed ADMM Family
children.top_down_role: Regularized variants that simplify local subproblems.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min_{x,z} f(x)+g(z)\) subject to \(Ax+Bz=c\), where \(f\) and \(g\) are proper closed convex and the block structure of \(A,B\) follows a communication graph. Let \(P_k\succeq0\) and \(Q_k\succeq0\) be block-diagonal local metrics.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous proximal or linearized distributed ADMM; regularizers are algorithmic quadratic terms, not objective modifications.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A regularized distributed ADMM iteration is \[x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_x\left\{f(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\|Ax+Bz^k-c+u^k\|^2+\frac12\|x-x^k\|_{P_k}^2\right\},\] \[z^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_z\left\{g(z)+\frac{\rho}{2}\|Ax^{k+1}+Bz-c+u^k\|^2+\frac12\|z-z^k\|_{Q_k}^2\right\},\] \[u^{k+1}=u^k+Ax^{k+1}+Bz^{k+1}-c.\] It is distributed when the metrics and coupling permit the two minimizations to decompose by agents or edges. A linearized member replaces a difficult quadratic coupling term by its affine expansion at the current iterate plus a local positive quadratic majorizer. Setting \(P_k=Q_k=0\) recovers unregularized ADMM whenever those subproblems are well posed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Regularized distributed ADMM adds local proximal quadratic terms to one or both ADMM minimizations. These terms stabilize or separate the subproblems without changing the underlying constrained objective. Linearized variants replace hard coupled terms with a local first-order model and a majorizing quadratic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The family is defined by ADMM residual accumulation together with block-local proximal or majorizing regularization in its primal subproblems.
equivalent_formulations_latex: A term \(\frac12\|x-x^k\|_{P_k}^2\) is a variable-metric proximal regularizer.
special_cases_latex: \(Q_k=0\) and \(P_k\succ0\) gives one-sided proximal ADMM.
immediate_consequences_latex: The regularization vanishes at a fixed point because \(x^{k+1}=x^k\) and \(z^{k+1}=z^k\).
boundary_notes: Indefinite proximal metrics require separate conditions and are excluded.
Regularizing the original objective permanently is not the same construction.
review_flags: An inspected source for the exact proximal/linearized distributed family is needed.
knowledge_statements.title: Regularized Distributed ADMM
Linearized Distributed ADMM
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linearized distributed ADMM replaces one quadratic augmented-Lagrangian subproblem by a proximal gradient step, reducing local solve cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize \((x^0,z^0,u^0)\). Linearize the quadratic penalty in the \(x\)-block and iterate
\[
x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\tau f}\!\left(x^k-\tau\rho A^\top r^k\right),
\]
\[
z^{k+1}=\arg\min_z\left\{g(z)+\frac\rho2\lVert Ax^{k+1}+Bz-c+u^k\rVert^2\right\},
\]
\[
u^{k+1}=u^k+Ax^{k+1}+Bz^{k+1}-c.
\]
In a distributed model, separability of \(f\), \(g\), and the incidence structure makes these updates local after neighbor communication. Stop using standard primal and dual residual tolerances; output \((x^k,z^k)\).
assumptions_latex: The problem is \(\min_{x,z} f(x)+g(z)\) subject to \(Ax+Bz=c\), with proper closed convex \(f,g\).
A primal-dual solution exists and \(\rho>0\).
The parameter satisfies \(\tau^{-1}I-\rho A^\top A\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The linearized primal subproblem is proximal and separable whenever \(f\) is separable; fixed points satisfy the original ADMM optimality system.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Function-linearized scaled ADMM for a separable linearly constrained convex problem.

notation.meaning: Current constraint residual before the primal update

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal Distributed ADMM
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Proximal distributed ADMM stabilizes or simplifies local subproblems by adding positive-semidefinite distances to the previous block iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\min_{x,z}f(x)+g(z)\) subject to \(Ax+Bz=c\), initialize \((x^0,z^0,u^0)\) and iterate
\[
x^{k+1}=\arg\min_x\left\{f(x)+\frac\rho2\lVert Ax+Bz^k-c+u^k\rVert^2+\frac12\lVert x-x^k\rVert_P^2\right\},
\]
\[
z^{k+1}=\arg\min_z\left\{g(z)+\frac\rho2\lVert Ax^{k+1}+Bz-c+u^k\rVert^2+\frac12\lVert z-z^k\rVert_Q^2\right\},
\]
\[
u^{k+1}=u^k+Ax^{k+1}+Bz^{k+1}-c.
\]
Distributed implementation uses block-diagonal \(P,Q\) and graph-sparse constraints. Stop at prescribed primal and dual residual tolerances.
assumptions_latex: The linearly constrained convex problem has a primal-dual solution.
The functions \(f\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, and convex, and \(\rho>0\).
The regularization matrices satisfy \(P\succeq0\) and \(Q\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The additional proximal terms vanish from the fixed-point equations, so fixed points satisfy the KKT conditions of the unregularized constrained problem.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-block scaled ADMM with explicit proximal regularization of both subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Regularized ADMM
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hybrid regularized ADMM linearizes a smooth objective component while retaining proximal metrics and exact augmented coupling in distributed subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize \((x^0,z^0,u^0)\). A hybrid regularized ADMM step is
\[
x^{k+1}=\arg\min_x\left\{f(x)+\langle\nabla h(x^k),x-x^k\rangle+\frac12\lVert x-x^k\rVert_P^2+\frac\rho2\lVert Ax+Bz^k-c+u^k\rVert^2\right\},
\]
\[
z^{k+1}=\arg\min_z\left\{g(z)+\frac\rho2\lVert Ax^{k+1}+Bz-c+u^k\rVert^2+\frac12\lVert z-z^k\rVert_Q^2\right\},
\]
\[
u^{k+1}=u^k+Ax^{k+1}+Bz^{k+1}-c.
\]
Choose graph-compatible block metrics for distributed local solves. Stop when primal and dual residuals meet tolerance; output the latest primal blocks.
assumptions_latex: The objective is \(h(x)+f(x)+g(z)\), where \(h\) is convex with \(L_h\)-Lipschitz gradient and \(f,g\) are proper closed convex.
The constraint is \(Ax+Bz=c\), and a primal-dual solution exists.
The metric satisfies \(P- L_h I/2\succeq0\), with \(Q\succeq0\) and \(\rho>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Fixed points satisfy the KKT conditions for the original composite problem; smooth terms are linearized while nonsmooth terms and coupling penalties remain implicit.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composite ADMM combining smooth linearization with proximal regularization.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The hybrid update is mathematically recognizable, but the exact condition P-L_h I/2 positive semidefinite is version-dependent and is explicitly marked unresolved. The cited broad sections must be inspected before accepting this parameter condition.

knowledge_statements.title: Local-Subproblem Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact local solves cost more per round; proximal or linearized solves reduce local work but impose regularization or stepsize restrictions. Their converged fixed points still satisfy the unregularized problem’s KKT conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the convex problem \(\min_{x,z} f(x)+g(z)\) subject to \(Ax+Bz=c\). A regularized ADMM local step has the form \[x^{k+1}\in\mathop{\rm argmin}_x\left\{f(x)+\langle y^k,Ax+Bz^k-c\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert Ax+Bz^k-c\rVert^2+\frac12\lVert x-x^k\rVert_P^2\right\},\] where \(P\succeq0\). Choosing \(P=0\) retains the exact augmented-Lagrangian subproblem; a positive block-diagonal \(P\) can make local solves separable or strongly convex; choosing \(P\) to majorize and cancel difficult quadratic curvature yields a linearized step. These choices change per-iteration computation and admissible stepsizes, but any converged fixed point satisfying the unchanged dual and constraint updates obeys the original KKT system.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, and convex.
\(\rho>0\) and \(P\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compares exact, proximal, and linearized local solves within two-block distributed ADMM.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The cited augmented-Lagrangian section does not specifically support the proximal-curvature cancellation, admissible-stepsize, and fixed-point claims for this regularized ADMM variant. The plain statement also asserts that exact solves cost more, whereas the mathematical statement makes no universal ordering.

knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Augmented-Lagrangian Frameworks
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A separable network problem can be represented by an augmented Lagrangian whose sparse coupling operator permits local and neighbor computations, followed by multiplier ascent on the coupling residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X_1,\ldots,\mathcal X_m\) and \(\mathcal Y\) be real Hilbert spaces, let \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_m)\in\mathcal X_1\times\cdots\times\mathcal X_m\), and define \(F(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)\). Let \(K:\mathcal X_1\times\cdots\times\mathcal X_m\to\mathcal Y\) be a bounded linear network-coupling operator and let \(b\in\mathcal Y\). For \(y\in\mathcal Y\) and \(\rho>0\), the augmented Lagrangian is \[\mathcal L_\rho(x,y)=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)+\langle y,Kx-b\rangle_{\mathcal Y}+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert Kx-b\rVert_{\mathcal Y}^2.\] A distributed augmented-Lagrangian framework performs an exact or specified inexact minimization of \(\mathcal L_\rho(\cdot,y^k)\), using the sparsity of \(K\), and updates \[y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho(Kx^{k+1}-b).\] When \(K\) is induced by a graph incidence operator, each component of \(Kx\) can be evaluated using endpoint or neighbor exchanges.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X_1,\ldots,\mathcal X_m\) and \(\mathcal Y\) are real Hilbert spaces.
Each \(f_i:\mathcal X_i\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex.
\(K:\prod_{i=1}^m\mathcal X_i\to\mathcal Y\) is bounded and linear, and \(\{x:Kx=b\}\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal L_\rho\) combines separable agent objectives with sparse network coupling, and \(y^{k+1}-y^k=\rho(Kx^{k+1}-b)\) accumulates the coupling residual.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Product-space augmented-Lagrangian representation of separable objectives with network coupling.

knowledge_statements.title: Augmentation–Splitting Relations
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an equality-split convex problem, primal ADMM and Douglas–Rachford splitting of the dual optimality inclusion generate equivalent iterates after a standard variable identification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For proper closed convex \(f,g\) and the split problem \(\min_{x,z} f(x)+g(z)\) subject to \(x=z\), the Fenchel dual optimality condition can be written \[0\in \partial f^*(-y)-\partial g^*(y).\] Applying Douglas–Rachford splitting to the two maximal monotone operators \(A:y\mapsto-\partial f^*(-y)\) and \(B=\partial g^*\), with resolvent parameter \(\rho>0\), is equivalent, after the standard affine identification of the splitting and scaled-multiplier variables, to ADMM applied to the primal equality split. Thus quadratic augmentation produces the proximal resolvents, while operator splitting permits alternating evaluation of the two component subproblems.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, and convex.
Strong duality holds and the primal-dual solution set is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The ADMM multiplier sequence is an affine shadow of the Douglas–Rachford sequence for \(0\in A(y)+B(y)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consensus ADMM viewed as Douglas–Rachford splitting of the associated dual inclusion.

notation.meaning: Fenchel conjugates of the primal objective terms.
Dual maximal monotone operators used by Douglas–Rachford splitting.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal H=\prod_i\mathcal H_i\), \(\mathcal G=\prod_e\mathcal G_e\), and consider \(\min_x f(x)+h(x)+g(Kx)\), where \(f=\sum_i f_i\) and \(g=\sum_e g_e\) are proximable, \(h\) is convex differentiable, and the block sparsity of \(K\) follows a graph.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A distributed primal-dual splitting is a fixed-point iteration for \[0\in\partial f(x)+
abla h(x)+K^	op y,\qquad 0\in\partial g^*(y)-Kx,\] that evaluates the resolvents of \(\partial f\) and \(\partial g^*\) separately and applies \(K,K^	op\), and \(

abla h(x^k)+K^	op y^k) igr),\] \[y^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{Sg^*} igl(y^k+SK(2x^{k+1}-x^k) igr),\] where \(T,S\) are positive block-diagonal metrics. knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distributed primal-dual splitting rewrites a composite network problem as coupled primal and dual monotone inclusions. It applies local proximal operations to nonsmooth terms, explicit local gradients to smooth terms, and graph-sparse linear coupling operations between node and edge blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Forward-Backward Splitting
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each agent communicates to evaluate a cocoercive coupling step, then independently applies its local resolvent. A stepsize below twice the cocoercivity constant makes the map averaged.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal H=\prod_{i=1}^m\mathcal H_i\) and seek \(x^\star\) satisfying \(0\in A x^\star+B x^\star\), where \(A=\prod_i A_i\) is maximally monotone and \(B\) is \(\beta\)-cocoercive. Choose \(0<\gamma<2\beta\), initialize \(x^0\in\mathcal H\), and iterate \[x^{k+1}=J_{\gamma A}(x^k-\gamma Bx^k),\qquad J_{\gamma A}=(I+\gamma A)^{-1}.\] Agent \(i\) computes \((Bx^k)_i\) from its local state and prescribed neighbor messages, then applies the local resolvent \(J_{\gamma A_i}\). Stop when a fixed-point residual such as \(\lVert x^k-J_{\gamma A}(x^k-\gamma Bx^k)\rVert\) meets tolerance, and output \(x^k\).
assumptions_latex: \(A_i\) is maximally monotone for every agent \(i\).
\(B\) is \(\beta\)-cocoercive and network-realizable.
\(\operatorname{zer}(A+B)\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(0<\gamma<2\beta\), the update operator \(J_{\gamma A}(I-\gamma B)\) is averaged and its fixed points equal \(\operatorname{zer}(A+B)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Product-space forward-backward iteration with local resolvents and a communication-realizable forward operator.

notation.meaning: Resolvent of the block-separable monotone operator.

knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Forward-Backward-Forward Splitting
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method uses one local backward step and two communicated forward evaluations, handling monotone Lipschitz couplings that need not be cocoercive.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(\mathcal H=\prod_{i=1}^m\mathcal H_i\), seek \(x^\star\) satisfying \(0\in Ax^\star+Bx^\star\), where \(A=\prod_{i=1}^m A_i\) is maximally monotone and \(B\) is monotone and \(L\)-Lipschitz. Choose \(0<\gamma<1/L\), initialize \(x^0\in\mathcal H\), and iterate \[y^k=J_{\gamma A}(x^k-\gamma Bx^k),\qquad x^{k+1}=y^k-\gamma(By^k-Bx^k).\] Each component of each evaluation of \(B\) is computed by the corresponding agent using the required neighbor exchanges, while \(J_{\gamma A}=\prod_{i=1}^mJ_{\gamma A_i}\) is block-local. Stop when \(\lVert x^k-y^k\rVert\) meets tolerance and output \(y^k\).
assumptions_latex: \(A_i\) is maximally monotone for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\).
\(B\) is monotone, \(L\)-Lipschitz, and network-realizable.
\(\operatorname{zer}(A+B)\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every fixed point satisfies \(x^\star=y^\star\) and \(0\in Ax^\star+Bx^\star\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tseng-type product-space splitting for monotone Lipschitz network coupling.

notation.meaning: Lipschitz constant of the forward coupling operator.

knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Fixed-Point Splitting
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A distributed primal-dual method can be represented as a relaxed averaged-map iteration whose components use prescribed neighbor messages; its fixed points decode to primal-dual solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal H=\prod_{i=1}^m\mathcal H_i\), let \(w=(w_1,\ldots,w_m)\in\mathcal H\), and let \(T:\mathcal H\to\mathcal H\) be an operator whose component \((Tw)_i\) depends only on agent \(i\)'s state and prescribed messages from its neighbors. A distributed splitting method has the relaxed fixed-point representation \[w^{k+1}=w^k+\lambda_k(Tw^k-w^k),\] where \(T\) is \(\alpha\)-averaged, \(\operatorname{Fix}(T)\ne\varnothing\), and \(0<\lambda_k<1/\alpha\). If a decoding map \(D\) maps \(\operatorname{Fix}(T)\) onto the primal-dual solution set, then \[r^k=w^k-Tw^k\] is a computable fixed-point residual, and every zero of this residual decodes to a network primal-dual solution.
assumptions_latex: \(T:\mathcal H\to\mathcal H\) is \(\alpha\)-averaged for some \(0<\alpha<1\).
\(\operatorname{Fix}(T)\ne\varnothing\).
\(0<\inf_k\lambda_k\le\sup_k\lambda_k<1/\alpha\).
\(D(\operatorname{Fix}(T))\) is the primal-dual solution set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r^k=0\) if and only if \(w^k\in\operatorname{Fix}(T)\), in which case \(D(w^k)\) is a primal-dual solution.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Represents a network primal-dual method as an averaged fixed-point iteration on product space.

notation.meaning: Map decoding fixed points into primal-dual variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Multi-Block Distributed Splitting
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block-diagonal metric separates the backward step across agents, while sparse cross-block terms are evaluated through neighbor communication.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal H=\prod_{i=1}^m\mathcal H_i\) and solve \(0\in Ax+Bx\), where \(A=\prod_{i=1}^m A_i\) and \(B\) contains sparse cross-block coupling. Choose a self-adjoint strongly positive block-diagonal preconditioner \(M=\operatorname{diag}(M_1,\ldots,M_m)\), initialize \(x^0\in\mathcal H\), and iterate \[x^{k+1}=J_{M^{-1}A}\bigl(x^k-M^{-1}Bx^k\bigr).\] Agent \(i\) obtains the neighbor blocks needed for \((Bx^k)_i\) and computes \[x_i^{k+1}=J_{M_i^{-1}A_i}\bigl(x_i^k-M_i^{-1}(Bx^k)_i\bigr).\] Stop when the product-space fixed-point residual meets tolerance and output all local blocks.
assumptions_latex: Each \(A_i:\mathcal H_i\rightrightarrows\mathcal H_i\) is maximally monotone.
\(M\) is self-adjoint, strongly positive, and block-diagonal.
\(M^{-1}B\) is \(\beta\)-cocoercive in the \(M\)-induced inner product for some \(\beta>1/2\).
\(\operatorname{zer}(A+B)\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The global resolvent decomposes as \(J_{M^{-1}A}=\prod_{i=1}^mJ_{M_i^{-1}A_i}\), so the backward computation is block-local.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preconditioned product-space splitting across local operator and variable blocks.

notation.meaning: Maximally monotone operator for local block i.
Cocoercivity coefficient of the preconditioned forward operator.
